features.name: Initial protective stop from structure or ATR, clamped and broker-valid
features.description: Every order carries a broker-side SL at the setup's invalidation level (opposite range edge, sweep extreme, swing) plus a buffer, or k x ATR read from the closed bar when no structure exists. Clamp the distance to min/max bounds, keep it beyond SYMBOL_TRADE_STOPS_LEVEL plus spread, round to tick size; skip the trade if the stop is too wide for the risk budget. Lot size derives from this distance.
features.rationale: Defines 1R, which the position sizer and every later exit stage depend on. Structure and ATR stops scale across volatility regimes and brokers; fixed-point stops do not. One or two parameters, so it is hard to curve-fit. Do not copy the per-signal or per-timeframe SL tables (7917, 17137) or the 10x-ATR stop with a hard cap (22705): they multiply fitted parameters or make the stop decorative.
features.gold_silver_notes: Gold's range differs several-fold between quiet Asian hours and US data releases, and absolute ATR scales with the price level, so fixed-point stops go stale. Point conventions differ by broker (gold quoted with 2 or 3 digits, silver with 3 to 5), so compute in price and tick size, never in 'pips'. Silver needs a larger minimum distance relative to spread because spread is a bigger share of its ATR. Stops gap on weekend opens and news, so size assuming slippage beyond the SL.

features.name: Take-profit as an R-multiple of the stop distance (or a structural target)
features.description: TP = entry +/- RR x |entry - SL|, sent broker-side with the order so risk:reward stays constant as volatility changes. Optional structural variant: range width projected from the breakout edge, or a fraction of the distance to the prior session extreme, with a minimum-room check that skips trades whose target is too close. Normalise to tick size and respect stops level.
features.rationale: A single RR input is transparent, testable and consistent with risk-based sizing. Structural targets with a minimum-room filter are a reasonable later variant. Avoid SL and TP taken from unrelated volatility measures (63916 notes the ratio must be re-tuned), forecast-derived or statistical targets (48097, 8397) and timeframe-keyed TP tables (12208): they add fitted parameters without supporting evidence.
features.gold_silver_notes: A broker-side TP is a limit order: it fills at the price or better and survives terminal outages, unlike EA-side closes. Keep the TP distance clearly larger than spread plus commission in price terms; on XAGUSD costs are a larger share of the move, so very small R targets are eaten by spread. Test RR on a coarse grid and require a plateau across neighbours, not a single peak.

features.name: Single SL modification gateway: tighten-only, broker-valid, step-gated, throttled
features.description: All stop changes pass one function. A candidate is accepted only if it tightens risk (buy: max(new, old); handle SL==0), sits on the correct side of price, clears SYMBOL_TRADE_STOPS_LEVEL and SYMBOL_TRADE_FREEZE_LEVEL, and improves by a minimum step (ATR fraction). Round to tick size, rate-limit per position, check the retcode, update the cached SL after success, cap consecutive failures and alert.
features.rationale: The most widely repeated and least controversial mechanism in the set. It makes every management routine idempotent and risk-reducing by construction, prevents invalid-stops rejections and modify spam, and has almost no tunable surface. It also blocks bugs seen elsewhere, such as a mode switch that re-stamps wider SL/TP on open positions (79181) or two routines modifying in one tick with a stale SL value.
features.gold_silver_notes: Metals tick very fast in the London/New York overlap and on news, so per-tick trailing without a step produces 'too many requests' errors. Express the step as a fraction of ATR, not points. Stops and freeze levels on metals can be nonzero and may change around rollover or news, so re-read them at each attempt instead of caching at init. If a spread spike makes a candidate invalid, skip it and wait; do not retry in a loop.

features.name: Staged exit pipeline with fixed precedence and profit-only trail activation
features.description: Run management in a fixed order: ensure a stop exists, apply forced exits (time, session, signal), then compute newSL = max(currentSL, breakeven candidate, trail candidate) for longs, mirrored for shorts. Trail candidates are ignored until they are beyond entry (or breakeven is done), so the initial stop is never tightened while the trade is negative and stages cannot fight each other.
features.rationale: This is architecture, not a tunable edge. It removes ordering bugs (trail acting before breakeven, routines overwriting each other) and makes behaviour deterministic and testable. The monotonic-candidate form (62732) needs no stored state, so it survives restarts. Many EAs reach the same result with flags ('trail only after breakeven', 'profit-only trailing'); the max() formulation is the cleanest version.
features.gold_silver_notes: On gold, tightening the initial stop before the trade is in profit turns ordinary retests of the breakout level into losses; leave the structural stop untouched until price has moved the activation distance. Express activation in R or ATR so the same pipeline runs on XAUUSD and XAGUSD without per-symbol point values.

features.name: Breakeven with net-of-cost lock offset
features.description: Once price has advanced a trigger measured in R or ATR (or after the first partial), move SL to entry plus an offset covering spread, commission and accrued swap (commission from deal history via POSITION_IDENTIFIER). Fires once: 'SL already beyond entry' is a stateless done-flag. Route through the tighten-only gateway; skip while the level is inside stops level.
features.rationale: Present in about 30 EAs, but popularity is not merit. The trigger distance is one of the most curve-fitted exit inputs, and a tight breakeven converts winners into scratch trades while flattering win rate. A profit-only ATR trail crosses entry on its own. Ship behind a flag (default off), trigger in R, and enable only if out-of-sample tests show lower drawdown without destroying expectancy.
features.gold_silver_notes: Gold routinely retests breakout levels and entry zones before continuing, so a breakeven triggered early is hit often. The offset must be in price terms derived from live spread and commission, not fixed points; on silver the cost offset is proportionally larger. Long metals positions usually pay swap, so include it for multi-day holds. Backtests flatter breakeven because the tester fills the stop at its exact price with no slippage.

features.name: Closed-bar ATR (chandelier) trailing stop
features.description: Trail SL at the best price since entry minus m x ATR, with ATR read at shift 1 from an iATR handle (CopyBuffer) so the distance is stable within a bar and identical in tester and live. Recompute on each new bar, activate only after a profit threshold in R or ATR, and send through the tighten-only gateway with a minimum-improvement step.
features.rationale: The best-supported trailing form, including the highest-quality gold EA in the sample (77691). One or two parameters, volatility-adaptive, monotonic, and when evaluated on bar close it is insensitive to tick-model quality, which keeps backtests honest. Best price since entry can be recomputed from bars since POSITION_TIME, so no persisted state is needed. Keep a disable flag so plain SL/TP is testable as a baseline; adaptive-width variants stay out of v1.
features.gold_silver_notes: Take ATR from the signal timeframe or one above: very short-timeframe ATR on gold collapses in Asian hours and makes the trail too tight just before London. Tight multiples are stopped by ordinary gold pullbacks, and silver's larger percentage swings generally call for a wider multiple; test a coarse grid per symbol. ATR jumps on news bars and would widen the candidate, which the tighten-only rule ignores.

features.name: Structure-based trail (Donchian or swing) behind a pluggable candidate-SL interface
features.description: On each new bar the SL candidate is the lowest low of the last N closed bars (or nearest swing/fractal, or previous-bar extreme) minus an offset; if it lies inside stops level, walk back to the first valid level. Implement every trail method behind one function that returns a candidate SL, so the gateway applies identical gates. Keep the method enum small.
features.rationale: Structure trails tolerate pullbacks better than a fixed distance and suit breakout or trend systems, but swing detection adds parameters (N, fractal width, timeframe, offset). The pluggable interface is good engineering; exposing seven methods (SAR, MA, fractal, percent of profit and so on) as optimisable inputs is a curve-fitting menu. Ship the ATR chandelier in v1 and add a Donchian channel as the single alternative later.
features.gold_silver_notes: Gold often wicks through obvious swing lows before reversing, so place the stop an ATR-based offset beyond the structure level rather than exactly on it, and use closed bars only. Silver's thinner liquidity gives longer wicks; a channel on the signal timeframe is less noisy than short fractals. An indicator line such as a Bollinger midline (11472) still needs the ratchet-only rule and stops-level check.

features.name: Scale-out ladder in R-multiples of original volume
features.description: Close fixed fractions of the ORIGINAL volume at R-multiple targets (for example part at 1R, part at 2R, remainder trailed or left to the broker TP). Use CTrade::PositionClosePartial with volume floored to SYMBOL_VOLUME_STEP; skip the stage or close fully if the slice or the remainder is below SYMBOL_VOLUME_MIN. Persist stage flags per position; optionally tie breakeven to the first partial.
features.rationale: Smooths the equity curve and appears in several of the better EAs, but it adds four to six parameters (levels and fractions), needs persistent per-position state, and typically raises win rate while lowering expectancy versus one clean exit. It is impossible at minimum lot. Add it only after v1 is validated with a single exit, and judge it on net R after costs, not on win rate.
features.gold_silver_notes: Small accounts trading 0.01 to 0.02 lots of XAUUSD cannot split at all; the code must fall back to a single exit instead of failing. XAGUSD contract size and lot step differ from gold, so normalise per symbol. Each slice pays spread, which weighs more on silver. On netting accounts partials reduce the single net position; track by POSITION_IDENTIFIER. Splitting the entry into several orders (919, 28117) only works on hedging accounts.

features.name: Restart-safe per-position exit state and strict ownership
features.description: Manage only positions matching symbol and magic. Prefer state derivable from the position itself (SL versus entry, open time, current volume); persist what cannot be derived (initial SL/1R, initial volume, partial stage) in GlobalVariables or a file keyed by magic and POSITION_IDENTIFIER, written on change. Rebuild in OnInit, prune entries of closed positions, never rewrite SL/TP wider or change a foreign position's magic.
features.rationale: Without it a terminal restart, VPS reboot or recompile silently changes exit behaviour (repeated partials, lost 1R reference, forgotten time stop) and live results diverge from the backtest. Cheap when designed in from the start and painful to retrofit. Stateless derivations (10984: SL-versus-entry as the breakeven flag) are the most robust form and should be preferred wherever possible.
features.gold_silver_notes: Metals bots normally run on a VPS across the daily break and weekends, where disconnects and restarts are routine, so exit state must survive them. Once the SL is trailed, the original 1R can no longer be read from the position; store it at entry. Order comments can be truncated or rewritten by brokers, so they must not be the only store (58462 encodes the timeframe there).

features.name: Time stop in traded bars, optionally conditional on progress
features.description: Close a position after N bars of the signal timeframe since entry, counted with Bars() or iBarShift from POSITION_TIME so weekends and market breaks do not count. Optional condition: only when the unrealised result is below a threshold in R (stalled trade), or only when at or above breakeven, leaving losers to the SL. Retry the close on later ticks until flat.
features.rationale: Bounds exposure time, swap cost and the chance of carrying a dead trade into an unrelated event. One parameter, stateless (open time lives on the position), restart-safe and easy to verify in the tester. Ship the simple unconditional form in v1; the conditional variants (71521, 73711) add a second parameter and belong behind a flag.
features.gold_silver_notes: Long XAUUSD and XAGUSD positions usually pay swap, with a multiple charge once a week, so stalled multi-day trades have a real carrying cost. A gold breakout that has not progressed within a few bars has often failed, and a bar-count stop captures that without another indicator. Count bars rather than hours because metals have a daily break and a weekend gap (62684 and 12220 correct for this explicitly).

features.name: Session-end / end-of-day flatten and stale-position cleanup
features.description: For intraday modes, close own positions and delete own pendings when the trading session ends: detect the in-session to out-of-session transition, and also close any owned position whose open date is not today so downtime is cleaned up. Use broker server time with a configurable cut-off placed before rollover; retry until flat.
features.rationale: Removes rollover spread blow-outs, swap and overnight gap risk for strategies that were only validated intraday. A single clock parameter, deterministic and easy to check in the tester. Seen in few EAs, but it is one of the cheapest survival mechanisms. A swing mode may disable it explicitly; the default should be flat at the cut-off.
features.gold_silver_notes: Metals spreads widen sharply around the daily rollover break and the weekly close, where a stop can be hit by spread alone. Set the cut-off comfortably before the break, in server time, and allow for the broker's daylight-saving shifts. Applying the same cut-off on Friday covers the weekend gap, which on gold can exceed any stop distance after geopolitical news.

features.name: Pending-order hygiene: bar-count expiry and OCO cancellation
features.description: On each new bar delete own pending orders whose ORDER_TIME_SETUP is N or more bars old (iBarShift), independent of broker expiration support. For straddles, when one side has filled or vanished, delete the survivor: react in OnTradeTransaction and re-check the per-side count of own pendings (symbol and magic) each tick. Also remove pendings when the session window ends.
features.rationale: Needed only if entries use stop or limit orders, but then it is mandatory: a stale breakout level triggers in a different volatility regime, and an uncancelled opposite leg creates an unplanned second position. Simple, deterministic, one parameter, and independent of which expiration modes the broker supports.
features.gold_silver_notes: Gold breakout pendings left across the daily break or a news release can be triggered by a spread spike and filled with heavy slippage, since stop orders execute at market. Brokers differ in the expiration types they allow on metals, so EA-side bar-count expiry is the portable choice. News straddles on gold frequently whipsaw both sides, so removal of the surviving leg must be immediate, not on the next bar.

features.name: Auto-attach missing protective stop (naked-position safety net)
features.description: Each tick, any owned position with SL == 0 immediately gets a stop: the intended stored SL if known, otherwise k x closed-bar ATR from the open price, clamped to stops level. If it cannot be placed after a capped number of attempts, raise an alert (optionally close the position). Log every occurrence; in normal operation it should never fire.
features.rationale: Enforces the invariant 'no position without a broker-side stop', the bot's main survival property. Covers market-execution brokers that refuse SL in the entry request, failed modifies and manual interference. It has no tunable edge, so there is nothing to overfit. Restrict it to owned positions; attaching stops to every position on the account (61119) is a manager tool, not bot behaviour.
features.gold_silver_notes: Some brokers execute metals in market-execution mode, where SL/TP must be set after the fill; an unprotected XAUUSD position during a news spike is the worst case for the account. Attach the stored intended SL price rather than a level recomputed from fresh ATR, so the realised risk matches what the position sizer assumed.

features.name: Virtual / stealth SL-TP levels hidden from the broker
features.description: EA keeps stop, target or trail levels in memory or chart objects and closes at market when Bid/Ask crosses them. The only defensible form is layered: a real broker-side catastrophic SL always in place, with the virtual level as a tighter inner exit. If ever built, persist the levels across restarts and log slippage against the virtual level.
features.rationale: A stealth-only stop vanishes when the terminal, VPS or connection fails, and it fills at market after the cross. The tester fills it optimistically, so results cannot be verified honestly, and several source EAs (17184) have no hard stop behind it at all. The readers consistently rate it useful only as an inner layer inside a hard stop; even that form should wait until after v1.
features.gold_silver_notes: During gold news spikes an EA-side close can fill far beyond the virtual level, and a disconnected terminal leaves the position unprotected exactly when volatility is highest. Spread widening at the daily break trips a virtual level evaluated on Bid/Ask just as it would a real stop, so stealth gives no protection against it.

features.name: Basket / aggregate exits (net breakeven, money target, basket trail, pairwise unwind)
features.description: Treat all same-side positions as one: compute the volume-weighted average price or net breakeven, then close everything at a points or money target, trail from that level, or unwind best/worst pairs. A correct version includes swap and commission, iterates backwards and uses a latch to retry until flat. Only meaningful for multi-position grid or averaging systems.
features.rationale: It exists to manage grid, martingale and averaging baskets, which hide risk behind a high win rate and have open-ended loss unless a basket stop exists. Money targets are not tied to market structure and are trivially curve-fitted. A one-position-per-symbol bot has no use for it. Keep only the reusable hygiene: P/L net of swap and commission, and close-all with a retry latch.
features.gold_silver_notes: Gold can run one way for a long distance without a meaningful retrace, which is exactly what destroys averaging baskets; most gold grid EAs in the sample carry low code-quality scores. A gold/silver pair basket (57272 suggests the reuse) is a separate spread strategy needing its own risk model. If an account-level cap is wanted, build it as an equity or daily-loss guard, not as a profit-target exit.

features.name: Secondary profit-lock ratchets, adaptive tightening and post-entry TP changes
features.description: Alternatives to an ATR trail: lock a fixed percentage of open profit, close on give-back from peak profit after a minimum advance, discrete tiered locks, 'noose' SL mirroring the remaining distance to TP, trail widths that shrink with time or R reached, money-denominated trails, and moving the TP after entry. If used, pick one, express it in R or ATR, and feed the tighten-only gateway.
features.rationale: Each is individually reasonable, but every one adds two or more thresholds and overlaps with the ATR trail; stacking them is a classic way to fit a backtest. Do not use the money-denominated versions (63569, 76605), fixed-pip tiers (17184, 8246) or TP manipulation (19963, 12208, 69651). If one is wanted later, choose a single ratchet in R and compare it out of sample against the plain chandelier.
features.gold_silver_notes: A percent-of-profit lock scales naturally with gold's large trend legs and needs no ATR tuning, which is its one real advantage. Tight give-back or noose rules cut gold trends short because deep intraday retracements are normal. Peak-profit tracking needs persisted state (best price or peak profit) to survive restarts. Money-based thresholds mean different things on XAUUSD and XAGUSD because contract size and tick value differ.

features.name: Signal-driven exits and verified close-then-reverse
features.description: Close on an opposite or exit signal evaluated on closed bars (opposite cross, channel midline for mean reversion, momentum extreme against the position), with separate permission flags for opening and closing per direction. For reversals use intent flags: close the opposite side, confirm no owned position remains, then open; retry until consistent. Signal exits run before trailing.
features.rationale: The verified close-then-open pattern (23220) and separate close permissions giving an exit-only mode (20885) are sound engineering and should be used wherever the strategy reverses. Indicator-specific exit rules (CCI extreme 12872, MA ladder 10848, profit-sign filter 25848) are strategy content with extra fitted parameters; they should arrive only with the strategy that justifies them, and always inside the hard SL.
features.gold_silver_notes: Stop-and-reverse on gold pays the spread twice at each flip and whipsaws in ranging Asian sessions, so require closed-bar confirmation. On netting accounts an opposite order nets the position; on hedging accounts it creates a locked pair unless the close is verified first, so check ACCOUNT_MARGIN_MODE. An exit-only mode is useful ahead of major news or the weekend.

features.name: Pyramiding into profit with capped adds
features.description: Add a unit only on a new bar when price has moved a step (an ATR multiple rather than fixed points) in favour since the last add, up to a small cap; never add against the move. Before each add, move the existing stops so total open risk of all units stays within the per-trade budget, and size the add accordingly.
features.rationale: Supported by a single EA (17065), whose reader noted it needs an ATR step and stop-to-breakeven to be robust. Adds raise the average entry, so a normal pullback after the last add erases open profit, and step and cap are easy to fit. Not for v1; consider only after the single-position system shows an out-of-sample edge, with aggregated risk accounting.
features.gold_silver_notes: Gold trends can justify adds, but its sharp counter-moves after extended legs hit the newest units first. Margin use grows with each unit, and metals margin requirements can be raised by brokers around news or weekends. Several positions per symbol need a hedging account or explicit net-position accounting on a netting account.

common_mistakes: Fixed point or pip distances for SL, TP, breakeven, trail and profit tiers (20/35/50 pips, 7.7 pips, 5-point steps) instead of ATR, R or structure units; they break across brokers' digit conventions for gold and silver and across volatility regimes. Readers repeatedly flagged 'would need ATR units'.
Deriving 'pip' size from hard-coded digits instead of symbol properties (point, tick size, tick value).
Trailing on every tick with no minimum-improvement step or rate limit, producing modify spam and 'too many requests' rejections on fast metals ticks.
Sending SL/TP modifications without checking stops level and freeze level (checking only the side of price, or nothing), and retrying failed modifies with no cap.
Management routines that can widen risk: a mode switch that re-stamps wider SL/TP on open positions, a take-profit pulled toward price or pushed outward after entry, trails that are not ratchet-only.
Hidden or virtual stops used as the only stop, with no broker-side hard SL behind them.
Breakeven set at the exact entry price with no offset for spread, commission and swap, so 'breakeven' is a net loss.
Breakeven and trailing written as independent routines that fight over the SL, or a trail that starts before breakeven or while the trade is still negative and so tightens the initial stop.
Using a stale local SL value after a successful modify in the same tick, and not handling SL == 0 (especially on the sell side, where 'new SL below old SL' can never be true for zero).
Reading ATR or other indicator values from the forming bar (shift 0), so the trail distance changes inside the bar and tester and live behaviour diverge.

Partial closes computed as a percentage of the remaining volume instead of the original, without lot-step normalisation, leaving dust below minimum lot, or without a once-only flag so a stage fires repeatedly.
Keeping exit state (partial stage, peak profit, initial volume, entry timeframe) only in memory so it is lost on restart, never pruning ticket lists, or relying solely on order comments.
Time stops measured in wall-clock hours that count weekends and market closures as holding time.
Polling a close hour every tick and re-sending close requests, or all-or-nothing basket close loops without a retry latch and without iterating backwards.
Relying on broker-side pending-order expiry, leaving the surviving leg of a straddle alive, or letting stale pendings trigger after the volatility regime has changed.
Assuming the entry order always carries its SL/TP (not true on market-execution brokers) with no check for naked positions.
Managing positions without a symbol + magic ownership filter, or stamping the manager's magic onto positions it does not own.
Close-and-reverse without verifying that the close succeeded, leaving unintended hedged or doubled exposure.
Basket money targets on raw floating profit that exclude swap and commission and do not scale with lots, used as the only exit for grid or martingale baskets that have no per-position or basket stop.
SL and TP derived from unrelated measures (band width for SL, ATR for TP), hard TP caps, or stops so wide (10x ATR) that they are decorative, making risk:reward accidental.
Parameter proliferation exposed to the optimiser: seven selectable trail methods, per-signal and per-timeframe SL/TP tables, multi-tier ladders, two-speed and volatility-interpolated trail widths.
Money-denominated trails and targets that ignore volatility and mean different things per symbol and lot size.
Judging exit logic by win rate (partials, tight breakeven) rather than net R after costs, and trusting tick-level breakeven or trail results from a tester that fills stops with zero slippage.

features.name: Closed-bar-only signal evaluation with new-bar gate
features.description: Evaluate signals once per new bar of the signal timeframe, reading only shifts 1 and 2. Detect the bar via iTime/SERIES_LASTBAR_DATE kept per symbol and timeframe. Run spread/session filters before marking the bar consumed, and if CopyBuffer/CopyRates returns too few values, set a recount flag and retry next tick instead of dropping the signal. Create indicator handles once in OnInit.
features.rationale: The most widely shared sound practice in this category (about 52 of the cited EAs read shifts 1/2). It makes every-tick, 1-minute-OHLC and live runs produce the same signals, removes repaint, and adds no tunable parameter. The recount flag (20943) and filter-before-consume ordering (62732) close the two usual holes. Bound the retry to a short period after bar open so the entry price cannot drift far from the signal close.
features.gold_silver_notes: Gold and silver have a daily trading break and wide spreads at rollover, so the first tick of a bar after the break can arrive late and at a poor spread. Detect bars by bar time, not by tick_volume==1, and keep separate timestamps for XAUUSD and XAGUSD and for each timeframe (the flaw the reader noted in 200).

features.name: Session/opening range builder from M1 bars
features.description: Compute range high/low from M1 bars between a session start and end (CopyRates or iBarShift + iHighest/iLowest), independent of chart timeframe. Convert window times from a fixed reference (UTC or exchange time) with DST-aware offset, skip weekend/missing bars, freeze the range when the window ends, reset daily, and rebuild from history in OnInit so restarts are safe. Optionally merge Friday with a short Sunday bar.
features.rationale: The higher-quality gold breakout EAs in the sample (75586, 76153, 78688, 78293, 17465) are all built on a session range, and the builder is the part that most often goes wrong: chart-timeframe dependence, raw server hours, weekend bars, state lost on restart. Building from M1 with explicit time conversion and a history rebuild gives a range that is reproducible in the tester and live. Window times are the only parameters; keep them coarse and do not optimise them finely.
features.gold_silver_notes: Natural windows for XAUUSD are the Asian range into the London open and the pre-New-York range. Broker server clocks differ (commonly GMT+2/+3) and US and European DST change on different dates, so windows fixed in server hours shift during the year. The daily break leaves missing M1 bars; a range built from too few bars should mark the day as no-trade. Use the same windows for XAGUSD rather than tuning per metal.

features.name: Closed-bar range breakout with buffer and entry window
features.description: Enter at market when the last closed signal bar closes beyond the frozen range by a buffer (ATR fraction or points plus spread), only inside a limited window after the range ends, with per-side enable flags and one breakout per side per day. A stricter variant requires the whole bar outside the range (low above range high). Never trigger on a bar-0 tick pierce.
features.rationale: Closed-bar acceptance beyond the range is the simplest trigger in the sample that is fully reproducible in the tester (market order at the next bar open, no dependence on intrabar fill modelling), and it filters wick fakeouts. Parameters are few: buffer and window length. The cost is a later entry and a larger stop distance than a stop order, but that cost is visible in the test instead of hidden. The whole-bar-outside variant (18704, 7612) is stricter but comes from lower-quality EAs; keep it as an option only.
features.gold_silver_notes: Gold routinely wicks through the Asian high/low at the London open before reversing, which is exactly what the closed-bar rule filters. The buffer must be ATR- or spread-scaled: a fixed point buffer that suits XAUUSD is meaningless on XAGUSD (different digits and tick value). After a long signal bar the entry can sit far from the range; check the remaining reward-to-risk (feasibility gate) instead of chasing.

features.name: Range-width and compression gate
features.description: Skip the day or setup when the reference range is too narrow or too wide. Express width in volatility units (fraction of ADR or ATR multiple), not fixed points; e.g. the Asian range must sit inside a band of ADR. Variants: NR-N (narrowest of the last N ranges), previous-session compression, re-arm only after bands contract again, and discard if the forming bar has already broken the range.
features.rationale: Stops and position size are usually derived from the range, so a degenerate range damages risk directly: too narrow puts the stop inside spread/noise and inflates the lot under fixed-risk sizing; too wide gives poor reward-to-risk. A two-bound gate in ADR/ATR units (17465 uses 23.6%-76.4% of ADR) is cheap and defensible. Keep the bounds wide and few. The NR-N, squeeze-latch and rising-but-capped-volatility variants add lookback parameters and belong behind a flag.
features.gold_silver_notes: Express bounds as a fraction of ADR or ATR so the same inputs hold when gold moves between quiet and volatile regimes and across both metals. Add an absolute floor relative to current spread (range at least several spreads), because silver's spread is a much larger share of its range. Holiday and pre-central-bank Asian sessions give abnormally narrow gold ranges; the lower bound skips them.

features.name: Higher-timeframe trend-side filter on closed bars
features.description: Allow longs only when a closed-bar trend state is up and shorts when down. Simplest form: bar-1 close versus EMA200 on the signal or a higher timeframe. Alternatives seen: in-EA ratcheting SuperTrend, Donchian-inset channel flip with hysteresis (SilverTrend), ADX with DI agreement, multi-timeframe slope agreement, confirmed-fractal swing sequence. Use one state source, read at shift 1, with an on/off input for ablation tests.
features.rationale: Present in about 18 EAs, including q5 77691 and q4 78968 (close on the EMA200 side). One closed-bar trend state removes counter-trend breakouts at low cost. The risk is that every extra filter or tuned period is a fitting knob, so ship exactly one, with a switch, and report results with and without it. SuperTrend, SilverTrend and ADX forms are interchangeable alternatives, not additions; rank-correlation (J_TPO) and Volatility Quality variants add complexity with no supporting evidence here.
features.gold_silver_notes: Gold trends persistently on H4/D1 but mean-reverts intraday, so take the state from H1-H4 or D1, not from the entry timeframe. Compute the state per symbol; silver often lags or overshoots gold. A price-versus-EMA200 state flips often while gold ranges around the average; the sticky channel-flip form (hysteresis between two bands) reduces that.

features.name: Setup lifecycle state machine with single-use latches
features.description: Hold each setup or level as explicit state: armed, awaiting confirmation, consumed, expired or invalidated. Rules: a level trades at most once; a setup expires after N bars; a close through a level deletes it; one entry per bar and per side; re-arm only after the condition resets. Derive 'already traded' from positions and deal history by magic and symbol so a restart cannot re-enter.
features.rationale: Duplicate and stale entries are a survival issue, not an optimisation: without latches a level retriggers after a stop-out and a restart re-enters. About 17 EAs carry some form (swept flag, consumed fractal, per-bar level latch, squeeze re-arm, per-direction latch), and the q5/q4 sweep EAs add confirmation windows with expiry. No edge parameters apart from expiry length. Prefer state derived from broker records (8417, 63916) over static variables, which several lower-quality EAs rely on.
features.gold_silver_notes: Gold revisits the same session extreme or prior-day high several times in a day; single-use levels stop the bot taking the same failed breakout repeatedly. Key latches by symbol and magic so XAUUSD and XAGUSD instances neither block nor duplicate each other. On restart, initialise as already consumed when the move for the current window is in progress (the guard in 11472).

features.name: Pre-trade feasibility and net-RR gate with logged reject reasons
features.description: Before any order, check as hard booleans: spread below a cap; stop and target distances beyond SYMBOL_TRADE_STOPS_LEVEL and the freeze level; net reward-to-risk after spread, (TP distance minus spread) / SL distance, above a minimum. Add the spread to buy-side entry and sell-side stop levels. If a pending price is too close to market, skip the setup. Log one reason string per rejected signal.
features.rationale: Hard feasibility checks protect the account from trades that cannot pay after costs and from order rejections, and they make every non-trade explainable. One parameter (minimum net RR) plus a spread cap. Drawn from 75652 (net RR and logged reasons), 8594/21452/71521 (stops-level checks) and 78688 (spread compensation). Prefer skipping an infeasible setup to pushing the entry out and shifting the target as 71521 does, which silently changes the strategy being tested.
features.gold_silver_notes: Spread on XAUUSD and especially XAGUSD varies several-fold through the day and spikes at rollover and US data. Evaluate the gate with the live spread at decision time, and test with real ticks and variable spread or the gate proves nothing. Silver's spread is larger relative to typical stop distance, so more silver setups fail the net-RR test; that is the intended result.

features.name: Two-sided pending stop bracket with broker-side expiry and OCO
features.description: Place buy stop above and sell stop below the range (offset by ATR buffer, spread, or Crabel stretch), each with SL/TP attached and ORDER_TIME_SPECIFIED expiry at window end. In OnTradeTransaction (DEAL_ADD), with a per-tick retry, delete the opposite pending once one fills. Replace, never stack, a same-side pending; abort if the delete fails; place nothing while a position exists.
features.rationale: Well engineered in the best sources (75586, 78688, 73711, 11350, 78308): broker-side expiry survives a disconnected terminal and OCO removes the whipsaw second leg. Kept behind a flag because a stop at the range edge fills on the first tick through the level, where slippage is worst and false breaks most common, and the tester fills it more kindly than a live server. If enabled, every hygiene rule is mandatory. About six news-timed straddles reuse the same OCO/expiry logic; those are counted under the price-chasing pendings feature.
features.gold_silver_notes: At the London and New York opens gold can trigger both sides within minutes; OCO prevents the second fill but the first stop is still exposed. Buy stops must add the spread (78688) because bid-based charts understate the ask. Check SYMBOL_EXPIRATION_MODE, since not every broker/symbol accepts specified expiry, and keep EA-side deletion as fallback. A stretch offset (78259) must be computed per symbol from M1 history.

features.name: Liquidity sweep-and-reclaim (failed breakout) entry
features.description: Keep a registry of confirmed N-bar pivots plus prior-day and session extremes. A sweep is a closed bar whose wick exceeds a level by at least k x ATR and whose close is back inside. Enter only if a bar within M bars closes through the sweep candle's body with range above an ATR fraction; otherwise expire. Each level is used once and removed on a true close-through.
features.rationale: The best-specified reversal entry in the sample: 77639 (q5) and 77094 (q4) implement it fully on closed bars with ATR-qualified wicks, confirmation windows and single-use levels. It is a second strategy with its own parameters (pivot width, wick multiple, confirmation bars, minimum range), so it should follow the breakout engine and be tested separately, not blended into it. Manually drawn levels (14206) cannot be backtested and touch-count clustering (71645) adds tuning; neither is needed.
features.gold_silver_notes: Stop runs through the Asian high/low and prior-day high/low are a recurring feature of XAUUSD around the London and New York opens; readers rated most of these sources at top gold relevance. Wick and confirmation thresholds must be in ATR units for both metals. This module trades against the breakout engine at the same levels, so define which module owns a level on a given day to avoid opposite positions.

features.name: Fresh closed-bar trend trigger: N-bar channel breakout or MA cross
features.description: Non-session trend entry. Channel form: bar 1 closes beyond the N-bar high/low built from earlier bars while bar 2 did not break its own channel. MA form: fast/slow sign change between bars 2 and 1 plus close beyond both the fast MA and the trend MA. The condition must be new on bar 1. An opposite signal closes first and reverses only if the close succeeded.
features.rationale: Simple and low-parameter. 77691 (q5, gold H4) shows the right channel form with a freshness test and no bar-0 data; 78968 (q4) shows the right MA form. Optional because v1 should carry one entry engine, and MA crosses lag and whipsaw on intraday gold. Useful as a transparent benchmark for the session engine. Adaptive averages (913), band-cross confirmations (48251/45323) and minimum-distance/slope/volume add-ons (62684) add parameters without evidence of benefit in these sources.
features.gold_silver_notes: Channel breakouts suit gold on H4/D1 where trends persist; on M5-M15 the same rule mostly buys session spikes. Channel width from average high-low range (48251/45323) or ATR adapts to both metals without point inputs. Silver produces more false channel breaks; expect a lower hit rate and do not compensate by tuning lookbacks per symbol.

features.name: Scale-free candle-quality metrics as confirmation
features.description: One helper returning ratios for bar 1: range/ATR, body/range, close location (IBS = (close-low)/(high-low)), wick fractions, body versus average body, tick volume versus its N-bar average. Use as a yes/no confirmation: impulse bar (large range, close near the extreme) for breakouts; rejection bar (long wick, small opposite wick) for reclaims. Treat zero-range bars as no signal. No point constants.
features.rationale: Ratio definitions (268, 324, 78343, 13901) are scale-free and transfer across instruments, and a single confirmation such as 'confirmation bar range above 0.3 ATR' is used by the better sweep EAs. But every added candle condition is another threshold, and pattern catalogues (three inside, morning star, engulfing) are not an edge on their own, as the readers noted. Allow at most one such gate per entry type, default off, justified by ablation. The tick-volume terms are the weakest part.
features.gold_silver_notes: Tick volume on XAUUSD/XAGUSD CFDs is the broker's quote count, not traded volume; it differs between brokers and between tester history and live, so never make a volume ratio a required condition. Range/ATR and close location are robust on both metals. Gold's news bars pass every impulse test and then reverse, so pair any impulse gate with the spread/feasibility gate.

features.name: Fair value gap / order-block zone retest
features.description: On each closed bar detect a three-candle gap (low of bar 1 above high of bar 3, or the mirror) larger than an ATR-scaled minimum; store top, bottom, midpoint, time and traded/invalid flags in a capped FIFO list. Enter when a closed bar dips into the zone and closes back in the trade direction. Invalidate when a closed bar passes through the whole gap. One trade per zone.
features.rationale: A closed-bar pullback entry with a registry, one-trade-per-zone flag and invalidation is implementable, but the dedicated sources are q2-q3, definitions vary between authors (gap size, tolerance, what counts as an order block, zone expiry), and requiring OB and FVG overlap (79285) multiplies the free choices. High curve-fitting risk. Consider only after the core engine is validated, with an ATR-scaled minimum gap and invalidation on closed bars (68125 evaluates it intrabar).
features.gold_silver_notes: Gold prints many small three-candle gaps on low timeframes in fast sessions; without an ATR-scaled minimum the registry fills with noise. Gaps formed across the daily break or the weekend open are data artefacts, not imbalance, so exclude bars adjacent to the break. Silver's wider spread puts zone-edge stops proportionally closer to noise.

features.name: Cross-symbol directional proxy
features.description: Derive a filter from other instruments: USD strength as the average position-in-range across USD pairs, the deviation between a synthetic price (e.g. XAUEUR x EURUSD, built from the correct bid/ask sides) and the quoted one, or the gold/silver ratio. If used, compute on closed bars with time-aligned data, require all symbols synchronised, and apply only as a veto, never as a trigger.
features.rationale: Supported by only three low-value ideas plus a 'macro proxy' term inside 75652's score, and the gold applications were suggested by the readers, not implemented in the sources. It adds data dependencies (several symbols, synchronised history, broker-specific symbol names) and multi-symbol tester complexity for an unproven filter. Defer. If tried, log it first as a diagnostic and promote it to a veto only if it helps out of sample.
features.gold_silver_notes: The economic link (USD strength against gold, the gold/silver ratio) is real but unstable intraday. Symbol availability varies: many brokers lack XAUEUR or a dollar index. A ratio filter between XAUUSD and XAGUSD also couples the two instances, which complicates per-symbol risk accounting and independent testing.

features.name: Oscillator zone-exit / band re-entry reversal trigger
features.description: Counter-move entry when an oscillator leaves an extreme between bars 2 and 1 (RSI back above oversold, stochastic/DeMarker crossing out) or price closes back inside a Bollinger/Keltner band after closing outside. Variants add ATR-adaptive thresholds, dual-oscillator agreement, divergence and zero-line qualifiers. The least bad form: zone exit on closed bars, only in the higher-timeframe trend direction, with a hard stop and no averaging.
features.rationale: Popular (about 22 EAs), but many hosts are grid, martingale or recovery systems (79021, 76605, 72278, 71700, 21511) where averaging down, not the trigger, produces the equity curve. As a standalone entry it fades moves in an instrument that trends hard, and it carries many thresholds (period, levels, adaptive steps, second oscillator, lookback memory) that fit easily. Not for v1 as a trigger. The zone-exit idea survives only as a possible pullback timer in the trend direction, later and behind a flag.
features.gold_silver_notes: In strong gold trends RSI and band extremes persist for many bars, so 'exit from oversold' fires repeatedly on the way down; silver's spikes are larger still. Fixed 30/70 levels behave differently by timeframe and regime, and the ATR-adaptive thresholds in 76605 are an admission of that. If ever enabled, require higher-timeframe trend agreement and a hard stop, and never pair it with averaging.

features.name: Weighted additive confluence score gate
features.description: Sum points or weights for many conditions (trend alignment, volatility ratio, spread, session, candle shape, touch count, volume, RSI depth) and trade above a threshold. If any part is kept, replace it with a short list of independent boolean gates, each switchable for ablation, and keep the reason logging. Weights and score thresholds should not exist as inputs.
features.rationale: Scores make weak evidence look like confirmation. Points and weights (50 plus/minus n, 0.3/0.3/0.2/0.2, 40/30/30) are arbitrary free parameters, the components are correlated, and a threshold on the sum cannot be ablated, so nobody can tell which condition earns its place. This is the most direct route to a fitted backtest in this category. Keep only what is honest in the sources: per-signal reason logging and the separate net-RR check, both carried by the feasibility gate.
features.gold_silver_notes: Score terms that look gold-specific (session overlap, macro proxy, ATR ratio band 0.55-2.2) are constants tuned on one author's sample. Gold's volatility regime shifts over months, so a score threshold fitted in one regime silently changes trade frequency in the next, and the same threshold will not mean the same thing on silver.

features.name: Price-chasing and stacked pending orders (news straddles, trailing stop-entries, stop ladders)
features.description: Buy/sell stops held at a fixed distance from price and re-pegged by timer or bar until an event, sometimes frozen minutes before release; a stop entry ratcheted toward price to catch a bounce; or ladders of stops at ATR steps adding positions as price runs. Any later use needs a modify throttle, broker-side expiry, OCO and a cap on aggregate risk across all legs.
features.rationale: Three variants of one weakness: the fill cannot be modelled or the exposure stacks. News straddles (7 EAs, all q2-q3) depend on fills during the widest spreads and largest gaps of the day, which the tester cannot reproduce, and re-pegging creates modify traffic and rejections. Trailing stop-entries (919, 11449) enter on a fixed-size bounce that a closed-bar reclaim confirms more honestly. Stop ladders, especially two-sided ones (26718), are grids by another name and multiply correlated risk at extremes; a one-sided add-on with a total-risk cap is the only form worth revisiting much later.
features.gold_silver_notes: XAUUSD around major US releases is the worst case: spreads widen many-fold, stops fill far beyond their price, and both legs can trigger. Brokers may widen stops/freeze levels on metals around news, so re-pegging can fail exactly when needed. For this bot a news window should be a no-trade filter, not an entry method. Silver gaps proportionally more than gold on the same events.

features.name: Self-optimising and learned signal generators
features.description: In-EA rolling re-optimisation of thresholds or lookbacks on recent bars, online pattern-probability tables fed by virtual trades (with exponential forgetting or asymmetric scoring), candle tokenisation, perceptron/network votes, and gating on virtual loss streaks. The reusable pieces are offline only: triple-barrier labelling and minimum sample counts, used in research with out-of-sample validation, not inside the live EA.
features.rationale: Adaptivity inside the EA is in-sample optimisation running continuously: it picks whatever worked over the last N bars with no out-of-sample check, carries hidden state that differs between tester and live starts, and makes results unreproducible. Sources are mostly q1-q3, and the readers themselves attach conditions (out-of-sample validation, minimum trade count) that the code does not meet. Per-direction parameter sets (8499) double the fitted inputs. Triple-barrier labelling (1229) is sound but belongs in offline research.
features.gold_silver_notes: Gold offers few independent regimes in any one broker's history and silver has thinner quality tick data, so learned tables see small samples per pattern and adapt to noise. A model whose state depends on when the EA was started cannot be compared between XAUUSD and XAGUSD runs or between backtest and live.

features.name: Tick-driven triggers: z-score bursts, renko bricks, intrabar displacement
features.description: Signals computed from raw ticks: rolling mid-price window returns converted to a z-score against a sampled baseline, price-move bricks confirmed when bid exceeds the previous brick by a box size, or a one-shot latch when price is displaced from the bar open by a threshold. If explored, scale thresholds by volatility and test only on real ticks with realistic delay and slippage.
features.rationale: Tick-window statistics depend on the broker's tick feed, on latency and on the tester's tick model; the same EA sees different tick counts live and in history, so results are not honestly testable. The self-calibrating z-score (77167, 77220, both q4) is well built and volatility-adaptive and the per-bar latch (244) is sound, but short-horizon edges are consumed by metals spreads. Out of scope for a survival-first v1; revisit only with real-tick tests and measured live slippage.
features.gold_silver_notes: XAUUSD tick density varies strongly by broker and session, so a fixed 'W seconds' window holds very different information in Asia and in New York. A 3-sigma burst on gold is usually a news tick with the spread already widened. Box or displacement sizes must be volatility-scaled; a fixed box suited to gold is wrong for silver.

common_mistakes: Reading bar-0 (forming bar) indicator or price values for signals, so the signal repaints within the bar and differs between tester modes; several raw ideas carry the reader's note 'would need shifting to closed bars' (21511, 8544, 8246, 17184, 13625, 68125).
Triggering on a tick pierce of a range or level instead of a closed-bar close beyond it, which buys wick fakeouts.

Thresholds in fixed points/pips (range width, breakout buffer, minimum gap, minimum distance from MA, oscillator-volume thresholds) instead of ATR/ADR/spread units; they do not transfer between XAUUSD and XAGUSD or across volatility regimes.

Session windows defined in raw server hours with no GMT-offset or DST handling, so the 'Asian range' drifts by broker and season; weekend and short Sunday bars counted into N-candle windows or producing trivially narrow ranges.
Building the session range from chart-timeframe bars, making the range depend on which chart the EA is attached to, instead of from M1 data.
New-bar detection with one static timestamp shared across symbols/timeframes, marking the bar consumed before filters run, or silently losing the bar's signal when CopyBuffer fails.
Latches and 'already traded' flags kept only in static variables, so a restart re-enters the same level, bar or expansion; no rebuild of range/setup state from history on init.
Levels and zones reused indefinitely: no single-use flag, no expiry, no invalidation after a true close-through, so stale levels trade days later.

Pending-order hygiene gaps: no OCO (opposite leg left alive after a fill), same-side pendings stacked instead of replaced, expiry handled only by the EA while online instead of broker-side, no handling of a failed delete.

Ignoring spread in stop-order prices and in reward-to-risk (bid-based levels for buy stops), and ignoring stops/freeze levels, leading to rejected orders or trades that cannot pay after costs; 'fixing' an infeasible entry by pushing it out and shifting the target.
Re-pegging pending orders every tick or bar without a throttle, generating modify spam and rejections right before news.
Fading the first touch of an oscillator or band extreme, and attaching oscillator entries to grid, martingale or recovery position management where averaging hides how weak the trigger is.
Weighted confluence scores with arbitrary constants (50 plus/minus points, 0.3/0.3/0.2/0.2, 40/30/30) that cannot be ablated and whose components are correlated.
Presenting in-EA re-optimisation, virtual-trade pattern tables or perceptron votes as 'adaptive' with no out-of-sample validation, no minimum sample count and state that depends on EA start time.
Treating tick volume as real volume in impulse, session-open and Force-Index style filters; on metals CFDs it is broker-specific quote count and differs between history and live.
Stacking many filters and separately tuned parameter sets (per-direction SL/TP, second oscillator, adaptive thresholds, extra MA confirmations), each adding a fitting knob without evidence it helps.
Immediate stop-and-reverse on the same tick, or opening the reverse position without confirming the close succeeded; implementation in the source (10848) was noted as unreliable.
Entering late into a move already in progress: placing breakout orders after the forming bar has already broken the range, or taking an expansion already underway after a restart.
Running opposite logics on the same levels (breakout and sweep/fade, or trend-inside and fade-outside envelope maps) without deciding which module owns the level, risking contradictory positions.
Relying on manually drawn chart lines or discretionary levels for entries, which cannot be backtested or reproduced.

features.name: Loss-at-stop sizing via OrderCalcProfit
features.description: Ask the terminal for the loss of 1 lot from entry to stop: OrderCalcProfit(type, symbol, 1.0, entry, sl, loss). Lots = riskMoney / |loss|. Use the real entry price (ask for buys, bid for sells, or the pending price). Floor to volume step, then re-run OrderCalcProfit on the final lot to verify loss <= budget. If the call fails or returns 0, use the fallback formula or skip.
features.rationale: The only sizing method in the set that does not depend on the EA author's own contract-size, tick-value or currency-conversion arithmetic. All five quality-5 EAs that size by risk use it. It defines the money lost at the stop, which is what makes every other risk limit and every backtest statistic (R multiples, % drawdown) meaningful. The verification pass after rounding (79017) is cheap and catches rounding or data errors.
features.gold_silver_notes: XAUUSD is typically 100 oz per lot and XAGUSD 5000 oz, but both vary by broker; the author of 77639 notes SYMBOL_TRADE_TICK_VALUE is wrong for XAUUSD on some brokers, which this method sidesteps. Also correct on non-USD accounts. The result excludes spread, commission and slippage past the stop, so real loss on a gold gap can still exceed the budget.

features.name: Tick-value / tick-size risk formula (fallback only)
features.description: Fallback only: lossPerLot = (|entry - SL| / SYMBOL_TRADE_TICK_SIZE) x SYMBOL_TRADE_TICK_VALUE_LOSS; lots = riskMoney / lossPerLot. Never divide by point or hard-code a pip value. If tick size, tick value or stop distance is zero, return 0 and skip; do not substitute a fixed lot. Log every time the fallback is used.
features.rationale: By far the most common method (about a third of all risk ideas), and correct when the broker's tick value is right, but it trusts a field that is known to be unreliable on metals. Keep it only behind OrderCalcProfit, as 78293 does; a v1 can equally just skip the trade when OrderCalcProfit fails. Hand-rolled conversion through a located FX pair (71657) and measuring tick value from an open position's profit (71700) are workarounds for the same weakness and add code that is hard to test.
features.gold_silver_notes: On metals tick size and point can differ, so any formula that uses stop points x tick value without the tick-size ratio is wrong (seen in 149, 40252, 19392, 24786, 22705, 46309; 11472 hard-codes pip value). Use TICK_VALUE_LOSS, not the generic tick value, and expect it to be stale or zero when the market is closed.

features.name: Never-round-up lot normalisation (skip below minimum)
features.description: lots = MathFloor(raw / step + 1e-7) x step, with decimals derived from the volume step, capped down to SYMBOL_VOLUME_MAX. If the result is below SYMBOL_VOLUME_MIN return 0 and skip the trade with a logged reason. Never MathRound, never raise silently to the minimum. One shared function for every order path.
features.rationale: Rounding can only be allowed to reduce risk. Raising to the minimum lot is the most common way a stated risk percent becomes false on a small account, and it is invisible in a backtest report. Skipping with a logged reason keeps the test honest: the report then shows the account is too small for the strategy instead of hiding it. The epsilon (79234) and step-derived digits (1397, 78343, 78308) prevent invalid-volume rejections.
features.gold_silver_notes: With a typical 100 oz contract, 0.01 lot of gold loses about 1 USD per 1 USD move, so a 10 USD stop needs 10 USD of risk budget at minimum lot. Silver is coarser: 0.01 lot of a 5000 oz contract is 50 oz, so a 0.50 USD stop costs about 25 USD. Small accounts will see many skipped silver trades; that is the correct outcome.

features.name: Guarded minimum-lot fallback with a second risk cap
features.description: When risk sizing gives less than SYMBOL_VOLUME_MIN, optionally take the minimum lot only if its real loss at the stop (OrderCalcProfit) stays under a second explicit cap, e.g. 1.5x base risk as percent of equity. Default off (skip). Count and log every use so the report shows how many trades exceeded base risk.
features.rationale: A controlled exception to the skip rule that lets a small account trade at all, with the excess risk bounded and visible. It is honest only if the second cap is tight and every use is reported; 78259 uses 1.5%, while 75652 allows 5%, which makes the headline risk percent misleading. Behind a flag, off by default.
features.gold_silver_notes: Most relevant to silver and to wide gold stops on accounts of a few hundred to a few thousand USD, where minimum-lot risk can be several times the base budget. If the flag is on, results from a small test deposit will not scale down linearly from a large one; test with the real deposit size.

features.name: Margin affordability pre-check with free-margin buffer
features.description: Before sending, OrderCalcMargin(type, symbol, lots, price, margin) and require margin <= k x ACCOUNT_MARGIN_FREE (k about 0.8-0.9). If it fails, skip, or floor down to the affordable lot and re-check; never round up. Margin is a ceiling on the stop-based lot, not a sizing method. Pause entries after repeated margin failures.
features.rationale: Prevents 'not enough money' rejections and keeps a reserve of free margin so an adverse move does not immediately approach stop-out. Seen in 19 EAs with buffers from 80% to 98%; the tighter buffers (98% in a martingale EA) defeat the purpose. Computing the affordable lot directly is better than stepping down one volume step at a time (63193). Do the check in one place, not duplicated at call sites.
features.gold_silver_notes: Metals usually carry higher margin than FX majors and brokers raise it around news, weekends and holidays, so check at send time with the actual price, not at init. A tight stop on gold can produce a risk-correct lot that is still unaffordable; the margin ceiling then decides, and the trade carries less than the nominal risk.

features.name: Aggregate exposure caps (total lots, positions, volume limit, pending reserve)
features.description: Before any order, sum volume of open positions plus pending orders on the symbol per direction, and across the EA's symbols. Skip or trim down if the new volume breaks: user max total lots, max open positions, SYMBOL_VOLUME_LIMIT (0 = none) or ACCOUNT_LIMIT_ORDERS. If pendings are used, reserve their OrderCalcMargin in the margin budget.
features.rationale: Per-trade risk says nothing about total risk when several positions or pending orders are open. A simple cap on positions and total lots is cheap and bounds the worst case; the broker limits (volume limit, order count) avoid rejections. The pending-order margin reserve (78308) matters only for strategies that place stop or limit orders and can stay off otherwise. Compute from positions and orders, not from in-memory counters.
features.gold_silver_notes: Gold and silver are both quoted against USD and usually move together, so a long in each is close to one larger position. The per-currency net exposure sum in 9356 supports treating XAUUSD and XAGUSD risk as one combined budget rather than two independent ones. Straddle-style pendings on gold breakouts are the case where the pending reserve matters.

features.name: Hard ceilings: max lot, max risk money, bounded risk percent
features.description: Independent ceilings applied after sizing: a MaxLots input (never above SYMBOL_VOLUME_MAX), a MaxRiskMoney per trade in account currency so percent sizing stops compounding past a fixed amount, and a compile-time maximum for the risk-percent input, rejected at init if exceeded. Caps only ever reduce size.
features.rationale: A last line of defence against a sizing bug, a bad tick value, a near-zero stop distance or a mistyped input. The absolute money cap (59001, 71521) also keeps long compounding backtests from producing unrealistic lot sizes that the market could not fill. Costs a few lines and has no tunable effect on the edge.
features.gold_silver_notes: A very tight stop on gold (a few tens of points) can turn 1% risk into a large lot whose real loss is dominated by spread and slippage; the max-lot cap bounds that case. Set the cap per symbol, since one lot of silver and one lot of gold are very different notional sizes.

features.name: Lot cap from remaining daily loss budget
features.description: Track realised plus floating P/L since the day start. Before entry, compute the loss at stop for the planned lot; if it exceeds a fraction (e.g. 80%) of the remaining daily loss allowance, shrink the lot to fit, or skip when the result is below minimum lot. A single trade can then never breach the daily limit by itself.
features.rationale: Seen in only one EA, but it closes a real hole: most daily loss limits are checked after the loss has happened, so the trade that breaks the limit is always allowed. Sizing the next trade against what is left makes the daily limit a planned bound rather than a reaction. Requires a daily loss limit and a clearly defined day boundary to exist.
features.gold_silver_notes: Define the day by broker server time and state it; metals have a daily break and the server day rarely matches a calendar day in the trader's zone. The headroom factor below 100% leaves some room for slippage on gold news spikes, but a gap through the stop can still exceed the limit. Count gold and silver against one shared daily budget.

features.name: Single pre-trade gate with logged reasons and per-day entry limits
features.description: One CanOpen(reason) function called before every entry; returns false with a logged reason code if: equity stop or daily limit active, outside session, spread above max, open positions or total lots at cap, entries-per-day at cap (count DEAL_ENTRY_IN in OnTradeTransaction and rebuild from history after restart), or the one-entry-per-direction-per-day latch is set.
features.rationale: Puts every refusal in one audited place and makes each skipped trade explainable in the log, which is what makes a test honestly reviewable. The per-direction daily latch (7612) and entries-per-day cap bound the damage from repeated re-entry after a failed signal. The thresholds themselves (max spread, session, entries per day) are parameters, so keep them few and do not optimise them finely.
features.gold_silver_notes: Gold and silver spreads widen sharply around the daily break, rollover and major US data; a fixed max spread in points must be set per symbol and is better expressed relative to the planned stop distance. One long and one short per day stops the repeated whipsaw re-entries that are common on failed gold breakouts. In-memory latches must be rebuilt from history after a restart.

features.name: Init-time validation of the sizing configuration
features.description: OnInit returns INIT_PARAMETERS_INCORRECT with explicit text when: risk-percent mode is selected without a stop loss; both fixed lot and risk are set, or neither; a fixed lot is off the step grid or outside min/max; risk percent exceeds the hard maximum. Fixed-lot mode stays available for testing but is validated once at start.
features.rationale: An undefined-risk configuration should not be able to start, either live or as one pass of an optimisation. Rejecting it at init removes whole classes of meaningless optimiser results (for example percent risk with no stop) and gives the user a clear message instead of rejected orders later.
features.gold_silver_notes: Volume min, step and max differ between brokers' gold and silver symbols and between symbol suffixes, so validate against the actual chart symbol at init rather than assuming 0.01. Symbol properties can be unavailable at init when the market is closed; fail clearly rather than continuing with zeros.

features.name: Loss-streak risk throttle (reduction only)
features.description: Count consecutive losing closed positions from deal history filtered by magic and symbol, so the state survives restarts. After N losses multiply risk by a fixed factor below 1 (e.g. 0.5 after 3), with a floor, and restore after a winner. Never scale above base risk. Off by default; thresholds fixed, not optimised; always report results with and without it.
features.rationale: Anti-martingale reduction can only lower exposure, so it is safe in the survival sense, and seven EAs carry some form of it. But it helps only if losses cluster, which must be shown rather than assumed, and its thresholds are easy to fit to one backtest's drawdown. The stacked version in 71521 (streak, win rate, drawdown, regime, hour-of-day P/L) is too many knobs to test honestly; the rolling loss-rate version in 8594 is a cleaner alternative. Keep behind a flag.
features.gold_silver_notes: Breakout and trend systems on gold tend to lose in runs during ranging periods, which is the case this targets. On small accounts a halved risk often falls below minimum lot, so the throttle becomes a trading pause; decide and document that behaviour. Count by magic and symbol, not by symbol alone as the standard sample (1921, 914) does.

features.name: Volatility-unit stop distance (ATR or gap-free mean range)
features.description: Stop distance = k x a slow volatility unit from closed bars: ATR(period), or the mean high-low of completed bars when session-break gaps should be excluded. Lot is sized from that distance, so money risk stays constant while lot shrinks in volatile regimes. Keep k and period few and coarse. Efficiency-adjusted units (stdev x (2 - efficiency ratio)) add parameters; leave out of v1.
features.rationale: A stop expressed in a volatility unit adapts to regime and price level with two parameters, and combined with loss-at-stop sizing it gives the same money risk on every trade. That is the minimum needed for a strategy tested over many years of changing gold volatility. The unit must come from closed bars and the lot must be sized from the stop actually placed (79181 makes this explicit). The KVR variant in 74840 is interesting but is an extra layer to fit.
features.gold_silver_notes: Metals have a daily trading break and weekend gaps; true range includes the reopening gap, so ATR on intraday bars jumps after the break. The mean high-low over many completed H1 bars (77060, about 20 sessions) is a steadier unit for intraday gold stops. Silver's percentage volatility is generally higher than gold's, so the same k gives proportionally wider stops and smaller lots, which is the intended behaviour.

features.name: Structural stop clamped to a volatility band, target as R multiple
features.description: Stop anchored to structure (opposite swing, a fraction of the breakout box or corridor height) plus a volatility buffer; the distance is then clamped into [kMin, kMax] x a daily volatility unit (ADR or D1 ATR), or the trade is rejected when outside. TP = final stop distance x a fixed R multiple. Lot is sized from the final clamped distance.
features.rationale: Only applies to strategies that have a structure to anchor to (breakout box, swing). The valuable part is the band: it stops a tiny structure from producing a tight stop and oversized lot, and a huge one from producing an untradeably wide stop. The specific constants in the sources (0.618, 1.382, 1.618, 61.8%) are arbitrary Fibonacci numbers; use round values and do not optimise them. Whether to clamp or reject is a design choice that changes the trade set, so test both.
features.gold_silver_notes: Obvious swing highs and lows on gold are frequently exceeded briefly before price reverses, so a stop placed exactly at structure needs a buffer in volatility units rather than fixed points. Box-height stops suit session-range breakouts (Asian range, London or NY open) that many gold EAs in the set trade.

features.name: Percent-of-price stop and target distances
features.description: Stop and target distances as a percentage of entry price (price x pct / 100), rounded to SYMBOL_TRADE_TICK_SIZE and checked against the stops level. Parameters stay meaningful as the price level changes over years. Use as a simple alternative to ATR stops, or as min/max bounds on a volatility stop.
features.rationale: Solves the price-level problem of fixed-point stops with one parameter and no indicator, which makes it easy to test honestly. It does not adapt to volatility regime, so it is weaker than a volatility unit as the primary stop. Most useful as a sanity bound on the volatility stop or as a baseline to compare against.
features.gold_silver_notes: Gold's price level has multiplied over the span a long backtest covers, so a fixed-point stop is a different trade at each end of the test. The sources claim the same percentage transfers between gold and silver; treat that with caution, since silver usually moves more in percent terms and likely needs its own value.

features.name: Broker stops-level and freeze-level floor applied before sizing
features.description: Before sizing, compare SL and TP distances with SYMBOL_TRADE_STOPS_LEVEL and freeze level plus current spread; widen to the minimum plus a small margin, or skip. Normalise all prices to tick size. Size the lot from the final widened distance so the risk budget still holds.
features.rationale: Avoids invalid-stops rejections, and the ordering matters: if the stop is widened after the lot was computed, the trade carries more risk than budgeted. 78778 widens first and then sizes; several others bump the stop at send time. A skip option is safer than widening when the required distance is far from the strategy's intended stop.
features.gold_silver_notes: Many brokers report a stops level of 0 for metals while the spread still widens to many points around the daily break and news, so floor the distance against current spread as well as the reported level (8397 uses stop level + spread). Freeze level matters for later stop modifications close to price.

features.name: Selectable risk base: fixed money, balance or equity; per-symbol virtual equity
features.description: Input chooses the money base: fixed money per trade (non-compounding, makes year-by-year tests comparable), percent of balance, or percent of equity (min of both is safest). Do not offer free margin as a base. Later extension: per-symbol virtual equity = baseline deposit + that symbol's closed and floating P/L, so gold sizing is isolated from silver results.
features.rationale: What the risk percent is a percent of changes both live behaviour and how a backtest reads. Fixed-money risk (78891, 71583, 72527) removes compounding so the equity curve and drawdown reflect the edge, not the sizing; percent mode is then a separate, explicit choice. Free margin as a base (149, 11472, and a mode in the 21361 family) shrinks and grows with open positions and is not a measure of capital. Virtual equity (611) is useful later but adds state to maintain.
features.gold_silver_notes: In a long compounding gold backtest the last strong trend dominates the result; fixed-money risk makes each year comparable. When gold and silver run in one account, a shared equity base couples their sizing; virtual equity per symbol decouples it, at the cost of rebuilding the figure from deal history after restarts.

features.name: Scaling size up by signal confidence, Kelly or win streaks
features.description: Multiplying the lot by signal score/100, by fractional Kelly from recent win rate, halving on opposing macro bias, or raising risk after wins (1.2x steps, up to 1.5x base). Each adds tunable parameters to the size dimension. Do not build; if ever tried, allow reduction only and compare against flat risk.
features.rationale: Variable sizing by score or recent results multiplies the degrees of freedom of the system and lets a backtest improve by concentrating size on trades that happened to win. Kelly from a small recent sample is extremely noisy and overstates the edge. The sources themselves mark the increase side as not advised (63193, 71521). Flat risk per trade keeps the test interpretable: every trade counts equally.
features.gold_silver_notes: Gold strategies typically produce few trades per year per setup, so there is too little data to estimate a per-score edge or a Kelly fraction. A fixed reduction for a counter-bias trade (as in 75652) is the only defensible form, and it should be tested as a filter question first: if the bias matters, consider not trading against it at all.

features.name: Lot sizing not tied to the stop (balance steps, drawdown budget, margin fraction, lot multiplication)
features.description: Lots from balance chunks (one minimum lot per X of balance), from balance / assumed maximum drawdown, from a fraction of free margin / margin per lot, or by multiplying the previous lot after a loss. None uses the stop distance, so money at risk per trade is undefined. Keep margin maths only as a ceiling.
features.rationale: These schemes hide risk: the same lot is used whether the stop is near or far, so loss per trade varies with volatility and the stated 'risk' input means something else. The drawdown-budget version (913) hard-wires a backtest's maximum drawdown into live sizing, which is curve fitting by construction. Lot multiplication after losses is martingale; a cap on the number of multiplications (21511) limits it but does not make it safe.
features.gold_silver_notes: On leveraged metals a fraction-of-free-margin lot can be many times the size a 1% loss-at-stop rule would allow. The standard library's fixed-margin money manager behaves this way too, so check what a library class actually computes before relying on it. Balance-step sizing does not react to gold's volatility regime at all.

common_mistakes: Using SYMBOL_POINT (or a hard-coded pip value) where SYMBOL_TRADE_TICK_SIZE is required, so loss per lot is wrong on metals where tick size and point differ (149, 11472, 40252, 19392, 24786, 22705, 46309).
Trusting SYMBOL_TRADE_TICK_VALUE without a cross-check; it is reported wrong for XAUUSD on some brokers and on non-USD accounts, and the generic value is used instead of TICK_VALUE_LOSS.
Raising a too-small lot to SYMBOL_VOLUME_MIN (clamp to min) instead of skipping, which silently exceeds the risk budget on small accounts, most severely on silver.
Rounding lots to the nearest step instead of flooring, hard-coding two lot decimals, or flooring without an epsilon so floating-point error drops a whole step.
Falling back to a fixed lot (or 0.01) when tick value, tick size or the stop distance is zero, instead of refusing the trade (74840, 71120, 71583, 28117).
Sizing from one stop distance and placing another: lot computed before the stop is widened to the broker stops level, or from fixed points while an ATR stop is actually sent.
Allowing percent-risk sizing with the stop loss disabled, or accepting contradictory inputs (both fixed lot and risk) without failing at init.
Using free margin as the risk base, so position size changes with whatever else is open rather than with capital.
Using margin (free margin / margin per lot) as the sizing method instead of only as a ceiling on a stop-based lot.
No margin check before sending, a buffer so thin (98%) it gives no protection, or stepping the lot down one step at a time in a loop instead of computing the affordable lot directly.
Ignoring pending orders when computing exposure and margin, and ignoring SYMBOL_VOLUME_LIMIT and ACCOUNT_LIMIT_ORDERS, so stacked pendings can all trigger into more exposure than intended.
No absolute ceiling: unbounded risk-percent input, no max lot, no max risk money, so a tiny stop distance or bad symbol data yields a huge lot.
Min-lot fallback with a generous second cap (5%) that makes the headline risk percent misleading, with no log of how often it was used.
Daily loss limits checked only after the loss, so the trade that breaches the limit is always permitted; the next trade is not sized against the remaining allowance.

Keeping loss-streak and entries-per-day counters only in memory (OnTrade counters) so they reset on restart, counting deals instead of closed positions, or counting by symbol without the magic number.
