Increasing risk after wins, scaling by signal score or Kelly, or multiplying lots after losses; stacking many adaptive multipliers (streak, win rate, drawdown, regime, hour of day) until the sizing cannot be tested.
Fixed-point stops and targets that do not scale with gold's price level or volatility over a multi-year test, and arbitrary Fibonacci constants treated as if they were tested values.
Reading ATR or range from the still-forming bar rather than closed bars, and using true range on intraday metals bars where the session-break gap inflates the unit.
Not verifying the final rounded lot's real loss and margin before sending, and duplicating the same check at several call sites with slightly different logic.
Treating XAUUSD and XAGUSD risk budgets as independent although both are USD-quoted metals that usually move together.

features.name: Daily loss limit on equity (closed + floating) with configurable day boundary
features.description: Block new entries (and optionally flatten) when equity falls a set % or money amount below the day reference. Loss = closed P/L since day start plus floating, net of swap, commission, fees. Day boundary is an input (server midnight or prop-firm reset hour); base selectable as balance, equity or the higher. Evaluate in OnTick and OnTimer; release only at rollover.
features.rationale: The most common protection in the sample and the one that most directly bounds a bad day. It is a risk-budget rule, not a signal, so it adds little curve-fitting surface if the limit comes from risk policy or a prop rule rather than from optimisation. Must be equity-based: the balance-only versions (77167, 77220, 56126) ignore open losses. The intraday peak-drawdown variant (74840, 63193: lock when equity falls Y% from the day's equity peak) is a stricter optional mode that adds a parameter; keep it behind a flag. Depends on the history-rebuilt reference, the persisted lock and the latched flatten to be trustworthy.
features.gold_silver_notes: Gold can move more than a typical daily budget within minutes around US data and FOMC, silver more so; XAUUSD and XAGUSD are strongly correlated, so the limit must be one account-level number covering both symbols, not one per chart. Check on a timer as well as ticks so a quiet chart does not delay the trigger. Metals have a daily break with spread blowout and swap rollover near the server day change; avoid snapshotting the day reference from equity in that minute.

features.name: Day reference rebuilt from deal history (deposit-aware, scoped)
features.description: Recompute day-start balance on every check as current balance minus today's trading P/L from HistorySelect(dayStart, now): sum DEAL_PROFIT+SWAP+COMMISSION+FEE of buy/sell deals; accumulate balance/credit deals separately so deposits and withdrawals shift the floor instead of counting as P/L. Optional magic/symbol scope. If history is unreadable, skip the check and count the skip; never guess a baseline.
features.rationale: Removes the single biggest weakness of the in-memory snapshot designs: a restart, recompile, VPS migration or a terminal that was off at rollover silently resets the daily baseline and hands the bot a fresh loss budget. Deriving the reference from the broker's own ledger is deterministic and works identically in the Strategy Tester, which keeps tests honest. No tunable parameters. Skipped checks should be surfaced in the status line; a conservative build can also hold new entries while history is unreadable.
features.gold_silver_notes: Metals carry meaningful overnight swap (triple on the weekly rollover day) and often commission on raw-spread accounts, so net-of-cost accounting changes the result materially. Use one account-level ledger across XAUUSD and XAGUSD; add magic scope only for reporting, not for the prop-style limit.

features.name: Total drawdown limit: static floor or trailing equity high-water mark
features.description: Permanent halt when equity breaches a max-loss floor: either initial/reference balance minus limit (static) or a persisted equity (or balance) high-water mark minus limit (trailing), in % or money, selected by enum. Update and persist the peak every evaluation. On breach: flatten own positions, delete pendings, set a permanent lock cleared only by explicit operator action. No automatic recovery release.
features.rationale: This is the ruin stop: the point at which the strategy is assumed broken and a human must decide. Both prop-firm rule types (static and trailing) are covered by one enum. The peak must be persisted; several sources track it only since EA start (71583, 8594) or only while flat (11585), which makes the reference depend on when the EA was loaded. Auto-release when drawdown recovers to half the limit (71583) defeats the purpose and should not be copied. The limit is a policy number, not something to optimise.
features.gold_silver_notes: A trailing mark on equity ratchets up on unrealised gold spikes that are then given back, so know whether the rule being mirrored trails equity or balance. Silver gaps and thinner liquidity mean the realised breach can overshoot the floor; pair with the early-trigger buffer.

features.name: Act-before-limit buffer on credit-free equity
features.description: Trigger every limit early: breach test is equity <= floor + buffer, with buffer as % of initial capital or the trigger set at e.g. 80-90% of the true limit, leaving room for slippage and gaps during liquidation. Use ACCOUNT_EQUITY minus ACCOUNT_CREDIT as equity. When unsure of the reset snapshot, take the higher of balance and equity as reference.
features.rationale: A limit that fires exactly at the threshold is already breached by the time positions are closed. The buffer is a one-line change with no fitting value in a backtest (it only makes the guard more conservative). Subtracting credit prevents a broker bonus from masking real losses. Choosing the higher reference when in doubt errs on the safe side.
features.gold_silver_notes: Size the buffer from the cost of closing everything in a fast market: spread plus slippage on total open volume in both metals. Silver spreads are wider relative to price and widen sharply at rollover and around news, so a buffer adequate for gold alone can be too thin when silver is open.

features.name: Crash-proof persisted lock state machine
features.description: Store lock level, reason, 'until' timestamp, day base and equity peak in terminal GlobalVariables keyed by login+server(+magic/scope), with a separate prefix in the Strategy Tester; GlobalVariablesFlush after each write and use a commit marker to detect torn writes. Daily lock expires by timestamp (stale locks dropped on restart); max-loss lock is permanent, escalate-only, cleared only by an explicit input. Other EAs can read the flag.
features.rationale: Every account-level guard is worthless if a restart forgets that it fired; 'needs persistence' is the most repeated defect note in the raw ideas. Best practice across the high-quality sources: until-timestamp instead of a boolean (78702, 79035), level that only escalates (79430), tester keys isolated from live (79372), commit-marker writes (79017), unlock input that then refuses to start (78702), and re-arm hysteresis after a manual unlock so it does not instantly re-lock (73870). Implementation caveat: terminal global variables are dropped after about four weeks without access, so a permanent lock should be refreshed periodically or mirrored to a file. Never implement the halt by simulating keystrokes (14773).
features.gold_silver_notes: Restarts and disconnects tend to coincide with the volatile sessions when the guard matters most. If gold and silver run as two EA instances, both must read and write one shared account-level lock so a halt triggered by one symbol stops the other.

features.name: Latched flatten with enforcement until flat
features.description: When a lock fires, latch a close-all state: close own positions and delete own pendings, re-running the sweep on every tick/timer until none remain (handles requotes, partial failures, closed market), reporting each failure. While locked, re-close anything new via OnTradeTransaction plus a timer, rate-limited to about once per second with throttled logging. Restrict to own magic unless run as a dedicated account guard.
features.rationale: A one-shot close loop leaves positions open whenever a single request fails; the latch-until-flat pattern (22827) plus event-driven enforcement (79372, 73870, 79035) makes the halt real. Pending orders must be deleted too, otherwise they fill after the flatten. The lock must also gate the bot's own entry path, or it simply re-enters. Rate limiting and log throttling prevent a retry storm. In a single-strategy bot, enforcement should cover only its own magic; closing everything on the account is appropriate only for a deliberately account-wide guard.
features.gold_silver_notes: Metals have a daily trading break and the weekend close: a close request then fails with market-closed, so the latch has to survive and retry at reopen. Emergency closes in fast gold markets need a generous deviation setting and must cover both symbols.

features.name: Stop-loss watchdog for naked positions
features.description: On every tick and at startup, scan own-magic positions for POSITION_SL==0 (or looser than required). Attach a protective stop at the configured distance, respecting the broker stops level and logging retcodes. Count consecutive failures; after N (e.g. 5) or a short grace period, close the position rather than hold unprotected risk. Alert on every occurrence.
features.rationale: Position sizing assumes the stop exists; a failed SL placement or modify silently converts a fixed-risk trade into unlimited risk. The best version (78343) escalates from re-attach to forced close, and 78982 adds a grace timer and alert. Restrict to own magic so manual trades and other EAs are not altered (8366 and 22001 touch everything). Auto-attaching a default TP is not part of protection and can be left out. No strategy parameters, so no fitting risk.
features.gold_silver_notes: Some brokers execute metals in a mode where the stop must be attached after the fill, and stops-level distances on XAGUSD can be large relative to a tight stop, so attach failures are a real path. An unprotected gold position during a news impulse can lose several times the planned risk in minutes.

features.name: Early-warning alerts and visible block reasons
features.description: One-shot alert (log/push) when a loss reaches a set share (e.g. 80%) of its limit; daily flag resets at rollover, total-DD flag re-arms only after falling below ~90% of the warning level; flags persisted. Every entry block and lock carries an explicit reason code shown in a one-line chart status and written to the log, throttled (e.g. once per 60 s).
features.rationale: Does not change trading behaviour, so it cannot be curve-fitted, but it is what makes the bot auditable: every skipped entry and every halt has a stated cause that can be reconciled between tester and live (75652's short block code, 79035's trigger reason). Hysteresis and persistence stop alert spam around the threshold. Push/email channels can stay optional; the reason codes and throttled log are the v1 part.
features.gold_silver_notes: A warning ahead of the limit gives the operator time to act before a scheduled release. With two metals sharing one risk budget, the status line should show which symbol consumed the budget.

features.name: Trade-frequency caps: daily/session quota, entry cooldown, one-setup-per-day key
features.description: Limit entries per day or session: counter incremented only on a confirmed fill, reset at the day boundary; minimum seconds between entries; optional day key (year*1000+day_of_year) set after a fill and after a rejected setup so a failed setup is not retried that day. Persist counters and keys, or rebuild them from deal history, so a restart cannot grant extra trades.
features.rationale: Primarily a runaway guard: it bounds the damage of a logic bug or a whipsaw that keeps re-triggering entries, and it caps spread and commission bleed. Keep the cap a generous safety ceiling fixed in advance; once it is tuned on a backtest it becomes a fitted filter, hence the moderate overfitting score. The skip-marks-day key (78293) is a clean way to avoid retrying a setup that was rejected for stop width or lot size. All sources keep counters in memory; that must be fixed.
features.gold_silver_notes: Gold breakouts around the London and New York opens often whipsaw several times; without a quota a breakout system re-enters on each. Costs per trade on silver are high relative to its range, so uncapped frequency erodes the account quickly.

features.name: Consecutive-loss breaker and post-loss re-entry restraint
features.description: Count consecutive losing closes from DEAL_ENTRY_OUT deals in OnTradeTransaction (profit+swap+commission < 0); at the maximum, block entries until the next day. Related rule from the revenge-trade detector: after a loss, for a set window (e.g. 30 minutes) forbid a re-entry with larger volume than the losing trade. Rebuild the streak from history on restart.
features.rationale: Sensible as a regime circuit breaker, but the daily loss limit already bounds the money at risk, and the streak length and cooldown window are easily fitted to past data. The size-escalation rule only matters if sizing can grow after losses; a bot with fixed-fractional sizing and no martingale gets it for free. Add later behind a flag, with the value chosen by policy rather than optimisation.
features.gold_silver_notes: Losing streaks cluster in gold's range-bound sessions, so the breaker does fire in the right conditions, but the best streak length differs between regimes and between gold and silver.

features.name: Exposure caps: positions, per-direction levels, single direction, entry spacing
features.description: Hard limits checked before every order: maximum total EA positions, maximum positions per direction, optional one-direction-at-a-time, and a minimum distance between same-symbol entries expressed in volatility units (e.g. a fraction of ADR) to stop clustering. Count from live PositionsTotal filtered by magic, not from internal counters, so the cap is restart-proof.
features.rationale: Bounds worst-case simultaneous open risk regardless of what the signal logic does, and is the structural barrier against drifting into averaging. The sources that have it are mostly grids capping their own levels (79021); for a stop-based bot the useful form is a low total-position cap plus spacing so repeated signals do not stack at one price (17465). Fixed by policy; the spacing fraction is the only value that could be fitted.
features.gold_silver_notes: Because XAUUSD and XAGUSD move together, same-direction positions in both are effectively one bet; the cap should count them together. Spacing in volatility units stays meaningful as gold's price level and range change, where fixed-point distances do not.

features.name: Account precondition gates: live-arming guard, minimum capital, margin level
features.description: Refuse or pause trading when basic account preconditions fail: OnInit returns INIT_FAILED on a real account unless an explicit allow-live input (or expected login) is set; no new orders while equity or balance is under an input floor; block entries when margin is in use and ACCOUNT_MARGIN_LEVEL is below a minimum. Floors are inputs, not constants; states persisted and reported.
features.rationale: Three cheap gates with no fitting value. The arming guard (27428, originally licence code) keeps an untested build off a live account. The capital floor stops the bot when the account is too small for minimum lot size to respect the risk rule (57272 hard-codes it; make it an input). The margin-level gate (78982) prevents entries that would move the account toward broker stop-out. Each should emit a block reason.
features.gold_silver_notes: Brokers commonly raise metals margin around major news and weekends and offer lower leverage on silver, so free margin can shrink without any price move. On small accounts the minimum lot on gold can exceed the intended per-trade risk; the capital floor should be consistent with the sizing rule.

features.name: Profit-target lock (challenge target / daily profit stop / equity ceiling)
features.description: When equity reaches a target (challenge target from initial balance, absolute equity ceiling, or daily gain % from the day reference), close own positions, cancel pendings and lock: daily targets until rollover, challenge targets permanently until a new starting balance is entered. Uses the same reference, persistence and enforcement as the loss limits. Off by default.
features.rationale: Two different things share this mechanism. A permanent lock on reaching a prop-challenge target is legitimate and cannot be fitted: stopping once the objective is met removes pointless risk. A daily profit stop is not protection; it truncates the best days, and the threshold is a classic optimised parameter that flatters a backtest. Ship the challenge-target lock behind a flag; keep the daily variant disabled and out of any optimisation. The 're-arm from new balance' form (58462) is just a repeating basket take-profit.
features.gold_silver_notes: A large share of a gold trend system's return typically comes from a few strong directional days; a daily profit cap removes exactly those. For a challenge account trading metals, locking at the target avoids handing gains back to a news spike.

features.name: Floating-loss circuit breaker (position and strategy scope, net of costs)
features.description: Secondary emulated stop behind broker SLs: each tick sum POSITION_PROFIT+swap+commission of own magic (per symbol and across symbols); if net floating loss exceeds a money or %-of-balance/equity-peak limit, or one position's loss exceeds a % of day-start balance, close via the latched flatten and lock entries. Set limits just beyond the planned worst-case stop-out so it only fires on gaps or failed stops.
features.rationale: In the sources this is mostly the only loss control of grid and martingale baskets (11585, 12220, 72278, 71645 with a 30% default), which is the wrong use. As a last-resort layer behind hard per-trade stops it has some value: it catches a failed stop modification or correlated losses across symbols. It is largely redundant with the daily loss limit plus SL watchdog, and it only works while the terminal is running, so it must never replace broker-side stops. Express limits in % of equity, not account currency. In MQL5 take commission from the entry deals, since the position-level commission property is deprecated.
features.gold_silver_notes: A combined gold-plus-silver floating-loss cap is the useful variant, since both can gap the same way on the same news. It does not help against a weekend gap any more than the broker stop does; both fill at the first available price.

features.name: Basket money / equity-ratio take-profit close-all
features.description: Close the whole basket when summed floating profit reaches a currency amount, a multiple of the basket money stop, a % of balance, or equity > balance x k; sometimes per direction, then re-arm from the new balance. Mechanically a tick loop over positions and a close-all. Typical of grid/martingale baskets; replaces per-trade exits with an account-level target.
features.rationale: Popular (11 EAs) but it is an exit strategy dressed as protection. It exists to harvest averaging baskets that have no per-trade stop, producing a smooth equity curve with an unbounded tail. Currency thresholds do not scale with lot size, account size or volatility, and the target is highly sensitive to optimisation. A stop-based bot should take profit per trade from its own exit logic; an account-level money target cuts across it and makes results hard to attribute. Only the net-of-swap-and-commission accounting is worth reusing.
features.gold_silver_notes: Several of these come from gold grid EAs. Gold's sustained one-way moves are what destroy averaging baskets, and a fixed money target tuned at one price level and range does not transfer as gold's level and volatility shift.

features.name: Equity / basket profit giveback ratchet
features.description: Arm once floating (or daily) profit exceeds a minimum; keep floor = peak profit x (1 - giveback%), raised only on new peaks; when profit falls below the floor, latch close-all until flat. If ever used, peak and armed state must be persisted and the scope restricted to own magic. Two extra tunable parameters acting on account-level P/L paths.
features.rationale: An account-level trailing take-profit, not a survival mechanism. The arm threshold and giveback percent are fitted to the path of past equity curves and interact with the per-trade exits in ways that make a backtest look better without adding robustness. One of the three implementations is described as broken (12641) and none persist the peak. If profit protection is wanted, trail the stop of the individual position, where the logic is testable per trade.
features.gold_silver_notes: Intraday equity on leveraged gold and silver swings widely on noise, so a giveback percent that looked right in one volatility regime triggers constantly, or never, in another.

features.name: Scheduled-event de-risking: Friday cutoff and pre-news flatten
features.description: Time-based protection: block new entries late on Friday (e.g. from 18:00 UTC) so nothing new is carried into the weekend gap; when a news window is active and own floating P/L lies within a small band around breakeven, close positions instead of carrying them through the release. Needs a reliable news-time source and UTC-correct clock handling; behind a flag.
features.rationale: The Friday entry cutoff is cheap, parameter-light and defensible; it could be enabled early. The pre-news flatten depends on an external event calendar and a breakeven band that is a fitted money parameter (58462 uses currency units), and the terminal's built-in economic calendar is not available in the Strategy Tester, so the behaviour cannot be honestly backtested without a separately maintained event file. Keep the news part out of v1 and never optimise the band.
features.gold_silver_notes: Highly relevant in principle: gold and silver react sharply to US employment, inflation and central-bank releases, and gap over weekends on geopolitical news. Spreads on both widen before the release, so a flatten should happen before the window, not inside it.

features.name: Grid-basket rescue devices (indicator shock exit, order-count sync, late-stage profit lock)
features.description: Three martingale-era patches: close the whole basket when M15 CCI(55) exceeds +/-500 against it; liquidate all remaining orders when the open-order count drops (one leg hit TP/SL); close the largest order once near the max-trades cap and in profit. They exist only to manage averaging baskets without per-trade stops.
features.rationale: All three come from the lowest-quality code in the sample (quality 1) and solve problems a stop-based bot does not have. The CCI threshold is an arbitrary fitted number that exits at the extreme of an impulse; the order-count trigger is a side-effect heuristic that breaks on any partial close; the late-stage lock is a patch on an exposure cap that should simply be lower. Adopting them imports the grid mindset and its hidden tail risk.
features.gold_silver_notes: Gold impulse moves push momentum oscillators to extremes routinely, so the shock exit would fire at the worst prices; silver even more so. Nothing here is specific to metals beyond the fact that these EAs were often run on gold.

common_mistakes: Keeping the day-start reference, equity peak, trade counters and lock flags only in memory, so a restart, recompile or VPS move resets the baseline and grants a fresh loss budget (flagged as 'needs persistence' on 72527, 76153, 71467, 77167, 79285, 8594, 78293, 61319).
Measuring the daily loss on balance or realised P/L only, ignoring floating loss (77167, 77220, 56126), so the lock fires after the damage is already open.
Leaving swap, commission and fees out of P/L sums, or matching deals by date without HistorySelect (56126), which understates losses.
Counting deposits, withdrawals and broker credit as trading result or as equity, which moves the floor in the wrong direction.
Triggering exactly at the limit with no buffer for slippage, spread and gaps during liquidation, so the real limit is breached while closing.
Computing a breach flag but never enforcing it, or leaving the wiring incomplete or broken (56126, 9499, 12641 trailing lock).
One-shot close-all with no latch or retry, no deletion of pending orders, and no entry lock afterwards, so failed closes linger and the EA re-enters immediately.
Flattening or modifying every position on the account without a magic/symbol filter (61319, 61119, 8366, 22001), interfering with manual trades and other EAs.
Auto-releasing a drawdown lock when equity partly recovers (71583), or implementing the halt by simulating keystrokes (14773), instead of a persisted lock that needs explicit operator action.
Tracking the 'peak' only since the EA was loaded or only while flat (71583, 8594, 11585), so a trailing drawdown reference depends on when the EA was started.
Rolling the day on the server calendar date only, with no configurable reset hour and no handling of a terminal that was off at rollover, so the day does not match the rule being mirrored.
Persistence keys that omit account login, server, magic or a tester prefix, so accounts, strategies or backtests overwrite each other's state.
Enforcing only in OnTick, so a quiet symbol or closed market delays the check; no timer or trade-event path.
Hard-coded constants and oversized defaults (balance floor of 1000 in 57272, 30% floating-loss default in 71645, 80% equity stop in 8594) instead of inputs sized from a risk policy.
Thresholds in account currency that do not scale with account size, lot size or volatility.
Using basket money targets, equity-ratio targets and basket loss cuts as the only exit for averaging baskets with no per-trade stop, which hides tail risk behind a smooth equity curve.
Treating daily profit targets and equity giveback trails as protection and optimising them, when they are fitted exit parameters.
Unthrottled logs, alerts and re-close loops that spam the journal or the trade server, and warnings without hysteresis that re-fire around the threshold.
Incrementing trade counters before the fill is confirmed, or not counting rejected setups, so quotas drift from reality.
Instant re-lock loop after a manual unlock because the trigger is not disarmed until the loss has receded.
Relying on a tick-emulated money stop or attaching stops late instead of guaranteeing a broker-side stop on every position, leaving the account unprotected when the terminal is offline.

features.name: Composite minimum stop-distance engine (stops level, freeze level, spread fallback, correct quote side)
features.description: One function returns the legal minimum distance: max(SYMBOL_TRADE_STOPS_LEVEL, SYMBOL_TRADE_FREEZE_LEVEL, k x live spread) plus a small pad, so a reported 0 never means 0. Measure SL/TP from the exit side (bid for longs, ask for shorts) and pendings from the correct reference per order type. Initial stops are widened outward before sizing; trailing candidates that violate it are skipped. Skip the trade if SL sits inside the spread.
features.rationale: The most common idea in the category (about 60 EAs) and here popularity matches merit: it removes invalid-stops rejections, which cluster exactly when spread widens. Keep k and the pad as fixed constants, never optimised. Two rules most sources miss: recompute lot size after any widening (62732 does not), and if the broker minimum would push the stop materially beyond the strategy stop, skip the trade instead of silently trading a different geometry. Percentage safety multipliers on a reported 0 (x1.2, x1.5, x4) remain 0, so the spread term is the real floor. Use a clamp helper for initial stops and a validate-only helper for trailing (19963).
features.gold_silver_notes: ECN gold feeds often report stops level 0 yet reject stops near price; XAUUSD spread widens several-fold at the daily break, rollover and news, so read the spread live at every use rather than caching it. On XAGUSD the spread is a larger share of typical range, so the spread term binds more often and tight scalping stops are frequently illegal or uneconomic. Fixed fallbacks such as 5 or 10 points (56773, 57020, 79181) are smaller than a normal gold spread and protect nothing.

features.name: Tick-size price rounding and instrument-scaled distance units
features.description: Round every price to a multiple of SYMBOL_TRADE_TICK_SIZE, not just _Digits; round stops away from price (floor buy SL, ceil sell SL) so rounding never makes them illegal, and size from the rounded value. Express distance inputs as percent of price or volatility units, converted through properties of the order's own symbol, never hard-coded pips or chart-symbol globals. Compare prices with half-tick tolerance.
features.rationale: Cheap, deterministic, and it is what lets one code base run on XAUUSD and XAGUSD and across brokers with different digits. Percent-of-price or volatility-scaled inputs also reduce curve fitting because a parameter keeps its meaning across price regimes. The name-based metal pip table (11449) solves the same problem but is brittle against symbol suffixes and broker naming; derive everything from symbol properties instead.
features.gold_silver_notes: Gold digits (2 or 3) and silver digits (3 or more) differ by broker, and tick size can differ from point on metal CFDs. Gold has traded from roughly 2000 to 4000, so point-denominated SL/TP, grid and trail inputs silently change meaning; percent-of-price inputs port to silver without rescaling. Read contract size, tick value and volume step per symbol; never reuse gold constants for silver.

features.name: Broker capability probe at init (filling mode, expiration type, account mode, input validation)
features.description: In OnInit, per symbol: derive filling mode from SYMBOL_FILLING_MODE bits and SYMBOL_TRADE_EXEMODE (pendings use RETURN), expiration type from SYMBOL_EXPIRATION_MODE (GTC else DAY), netting vs hedging from ACCOUNT_MARGIN_MODE, set magic and deviation, cache results. Validate inputs against volume min/max/step and stops level and return INIT_PARAMETERS_INCORRECT on violation. On an unsupported-filling retcode, try the remaining modes once and remember the one that worked.
features.rationale: Hard-coded FOK/IOC is the single most frequent cause of an EA that simply never trades on a new broker. CTrade::SetTypeFillingBySymbol plus SetMarginMode covers the simple case; the bitmask plus execution-mode derivation (63916, 26324) is the more complete version. Failing fast at init with an explicit message is better than discovering a bad lot or filling mode at the first signal. No tunable parameters, so no fitting risk.
features.gold_silver_notes: Metal symbols frequently carry a different filling policy and expiration mode than the same broker's FX pairs, and XAUUSD and XAGUSD can differ from each other; probe each symbol separately. The emergency close path must use the same detected filling mode (67011 cascades FOK, IOC, RETURN on close for exactly this reason).

features.name: Pre-trade permission and broker-limit gate with distinct reason codes
features.description: A single CanSend() run before every entry, in order: terminal/EA/account trade permissions and connection, expected ACCOUNT_LOGIN, SYMBOL_TRADE_MODE allows this direction (full/long-only/short-only/close-only), ACCOUNT_LIMIT_ORDERS, same-side positions plus pendings versus SYMBOL_VOLUME_LIMIT, spread cap. Each failure returns a distinct enum value that is logged once per change, so every skipped trade has a recorded reason. Never applied to closing orders.
features.rationale: Turns broker rejections into deliberate, explained skips, which is what makes live-versus-backtest differences diagnosable. The custom error enum from the cTrade pipelines (26451, 26418, 26315, 26324) is the valuable part: without reason codes a gate is just a silent filter. Keep it purely about permissions and limits; do not let strategy filters creep into it.
features.gold_silver_notes: Brokers can switch metals to close-only around holidays or extreme volatility and often set small per-symbol volume limits on XAU/XAG; the gate must report this instead of spamming rejected entries. Investor-password or disabled-account states should be detected once, not on every tick.

features.name: Volume normalisation and margin affordability check
features.description: Floor the risk-sized lot to SYMBOL_VOLUME_STEP (decimals derived from the step), clamp to min/max, and log when the traded lot differs from the requested one. Then OrderCalcMargin for the exact type/price must fit free margin with a reserve; if not, or if the call fails, skip (or step the lot down, never up). Partial closes: floor to step and close everything if the remainder would be below minimum lot.
features.rationale: Seen in about 54 EAs and genuinely necessary, but with a survival caveat: the lot must come from risk sizing and margin may only ever reduce it. If the risk-sized lot is below the minimum lot, skip the trade; falling back to minimum lot (62248) silently exceeds the risk budget. Fail closed when OrderCalcMargin itself fails (77180). Announcing the clamp with its size multiple (77060) keeps risk honest. The margin reserve is a fixed constant, not an optimisation input.
features.gold_silver_notes: On small accounts the minimum gold lot with a volatility-sized stop can already exceed the per-trade risk budget, so the skip rule matters more than on FX. Silver's contract is typically much larger per lot than gold's, so one volume step moves risk in coarser jumps; size each metal from its own tick value and step. Brokers can raise metal margin around weekends and major events, so always compute margin live with OrderCalcMargin instead of deriving it from leverage.

features.name: OrderCheck preflight inside the send path
features.description: Subclass CTrade (or wrap OrderSend) so every request first runs OrderCheck on the exact MqlTradeRequest; reject on a non-zero retcode or negative post-trade free margin and log retcode, comment and margin figures. Requests that close or reduce a position are always let through, even if the check reports no money. A failed check must abort the send, not merely be logged.
features.rationale: A free server-rule simulation that catches margin, volume and stop errors before they reach the broker. Putting it in an overridden OrderSend (78968) guarantees no code path can bypass it, and the close/reduce exemption is essential: a preflight must never block an exit. It complements rather than replaces the stop-distance and session gates, since market-closed and frozen states only surface at send time.
features.gold_silver_notes: Useful on metals because margin requirements and stop rules differ from FX and can change between sessions; the logged check comment tells you which rule changed. Verify the exemption for reducing orders on a low-margin gold account, where a full close can otherwise be refused by your own check.

features.name: Market-availability gate: broker session table, quote freshness, data readiness
features.description: Before any entry or modify: tick valid (bid>0, ask>=bid), quote age versus TimeTradeServer below a limit, server time inside a SymbolInfoSessionTrade window for the weekday (handling sessions that wrap midnight), indicator CopyBuffer returned exactly the requested count. Block new entries N minutes before session end and pull time exits forward to before the close. Compute spread from validated bid/ask.
features.rationale: Avoids acting on empty or stale quotes after reconnects and stops the EA from hammering a closed market. Reading the broker's own session table is more robust than hard-coded hours and handles DST and broker differences. Keep the pre-close cutoff a fixed constant (15 minutes in 77639), not an optimised input. The quote-age test must be neutral in the Strategy Tester, where ticks are synthetic, so it does not create a live/backtest difference.
features.gold_silver_notes: Metals have a daily trading break and a weekend gap, and spread is at its worst right around them: entries just before the break carry gap risk with no ability to exit, and time-based exits scheduled at the close can be blocked by freeze rules. Silver session windows can differ from gold at some brokers, so read the table per symbol. Apply the same gate to trailing/breakeven modifications to avoid market-closed rejections.

features.name: Protected entry: stops anchored to the real fill, fail-safe close, slippage tolerance
features.description: Invariant: no position survives without a confirmed server-side SL. Send the stop in the entry request when the broker accepts it; otherwise send naked, find the position via DEAL_POSITION_ID, and attach. Either way, after the fill recompute TP (R multiple) and risk from the actual price; if the modify fails after bounded retries, close immediately. Skip the entry when price has drifted beyond tolerance from the signal price.
features.rationale: The fail-safe close is what separates the good implementations (77639, 77691, 77167, 77220) from the many two-step entries that never check the modify (27964, 10925, 17373, 913). Prefer the atomic form where possible because the naked window is itself a risk; use two-step only as a fallback for brokers that reject stops on market execution. Pick one re-anchoring rule (SL at planned level with TP recomputed, or constant distance as in 71583) and use the same path in tester and live. A dynamic deviation equal to current spread (611) is a minor addition; the drift guard (14085) does the real work.
features.gold_silver_notes: Gold market orders can slip by a meaningful fraction of a tight stop during spikes, so risk computed from the intended entry is wrong after the fill; re-anchoring keeps R honest. Under market execution, common for metals at ECN brokers, the deviation field is not a reliable limit, so the pre-send drift check and the post-fill risk check are the real protection. A naked gold position during a news spike is the worst case this invariant exists to prevent.

features.name: Safe modify/close wrapper: freeze-level guard, no-change skip, minimum step, throttle
features.description: All SL/TP modifies, closes and pending deletes pass one wrapper: re-select ticket and verify symbol+magic; skip if the existing level or order price is inside the freeze zone (retry later, log once per ticket); skip if the change is under half a tick or below a minimum improvement step; never loosen a stop; rate-limit per ticket and refuse retries for some seconds after a failure.
features.rationale: Trailing and breakeven loops are the main source of request spam and TOO_MANY_REQUESTS/NO_CHANGES errors; this wrapper removes them without changing strategy logic. The freeze check must look at the existing level first (46309), since the server refuses modification of a frozen order regardless of the new value. Express the minimum step as a volatility fraction or tick multiple with a fixed value; do not optimise it. Emergency closes may bypass the throttle but not the freeze check.
features.gold_silver_notes: Gold ticks arrive very fast, so an unthrottled per-tick trail can issue hundreds of modifies in a volatile minute. Fixed pip steps (2 pips in 71077) are instrument-specific and should be scaled for XAU and XAG separately. Where a broker sets a non-zero freeze level on metals, closes near SL/TP can be refused, which is another reason to start time exits before the session end.

features.name: Retcode-classified retry and backoff with attempt budgets
features.description: Map every trade retcode to a class: transient (REQUOTE, PRICE_CHANGED, PRICE_OFF, TOO_MANY_REQUESTS, busy/timeout: refresh quote, bounded retries, short randomised pause), wait-state (MARKET_CLOSED, TRADE_DISABLED, FROZEN: timed backoff of a minute or more), non-retryable (invalid stops/volume, no money: give up, log) and fatal (account disabled: halt EA, alert). Entries get one bounded attempt per signal; protective exits persist until confirmed.
features.rationale: A table-driven policy replaces both failure modes seen in the sources: unbounded retry loops (14833, 14869) and every-tick resending of a failing entry (fixed in 77060 by stamping the attempt before sending). The asymmetry is deliberate: a missed entry costs nothing, an unexecuted exit can cost the account. Implement backoff with timestamps (retry_after per ticket, as in 79017 and 70900), not long Sleep calls inside the tick handler as in the MT4-era wrappers. Before any entry retry, re-run the spread and drift checks.
features.gold_silver_notes: MARKET_CLOSED appears every day at the metals break and over the weekend; without a backoff the EA floods the server and the log. Requotes and off-quotes cluster around news spikes, which is precisely when a retried gold entry gets the worst price, so entry retries must be few and re-validated.

features.name: Read-back confirmation of fills, modifies and closes
features.description: Never trust a boolean return. Accept only DONE, PLACED or DONE_PARTIAL and require ResultDeal/ResultOrder non-zero; then re-select the position and compare stored SL/TP with the request within tick tolerance, and after a close verify the position is gone before counting the exit. Track filled versus requested volume for partial fills. Clear the signal/state flag only after confirmation; otherwise re-check on later ticks or OnTradeTransaction.
features.rationale: The EA's internal state (position count, daily trade counter, risk used) is only as honest as its confirmation step. 78343's read-back for SL and close is the cleanest version; 12220's deal-count polling solves the same problem with Sleep and should be replaced by OnTradeTransaction or next-tick re-checks. Risk accounting must use the filled volume, not the requested one.
features.gold_silver_notes: With IOC filling on thinner metal liquidity, especially silver and off-hours gold, partial fills are possible; the stop and risk bookkeeping must match the actual volume. A stop modification that silently did not apply is far more expensive on gold than on a slow FX pair.

features.name: Duplicate-entry prevention and restart-safe ownership
features.description: Before sending: scan positions by magic+symbol via ticket (restart-safe), scan OrdersTotal for an own market order still in flight (no position id yet), and after a timeout check whether a matching position opened at or after the request time before retrying. Add a short post-fill cooldown stamped from OnTradeTransaction, one entry per bar/signal, and a cap on sends per second with an auto-expiring in-progress flag.
features.rationale: Double entries are a classic silent risk multiplier and come from three distinct causes that each need their own guard: async fill latency (in-flight check, 26418/26315), timeouts followed by blind retry (9086), and restarts that lose in-memory state (78715). Keep cooldowns short and execution-only so they do not become an untested strategy filter. The MT4 GlobalVariable trade-context mutex (7876) is not needed in MT5; a shared lock is only relevant if several EAs draw on one risk budget.
features.gold_silver_notes: Gold delivers many ticks between sending an order and the position becoming visible, so a naive PositionsTotal()==0 test re-fires easily. If the same bot instance set trades both XAUUSD and XAGUSD, ownership and counters must be keyed by symbol plus magic, because the two metals are strongly correlated and an accidental duplicate compounds an already concentrated exposure.

features.name: Emergency flatten routine (snapshot, pendings first, retry until flat)
features.description: A dedicated 'get flat' path used by risk halts: snapshot tickets into arrays first, delete pendings before closing positions (so nothing fills mid-flatten), close by position ticket with per-symbol filling mode, one retry on requote, backoff on market-closed/trade-disabled, about one round per second, repeat until the in-scope count is zero, report leftovers and alert if still not flat after 30+ seconds. Abort the sweep on fatal retcodes.
features.rationale: A daily-loss or kill-switch rule is only real if the flatten path is robust; the two quality-5 guards (78702, 79035) show the needed pieces: stable ticket snapshot, pendings before positions, persistence while halted, rate limiting and an alert when it cannot finish. Closing by position ticket (62811) is hedging-safe. No tunable strategy parameters.
features.gold_silver_notes: If a halt triggers during the metals daily break or the weekend, nothing can be closed until reopen, so the server-side stop on every position remains the true protection and the loop must resume automatically at the open. Deleting pending breakout orders first matters on gold, where a spike during the flatten can fill a leftover stop order.

features.name: Pending-order lifecycle hygiene (side validity, spread-adjusted trigger, expiry, OCO)
features.description: For stop/limit entries: validate entry distance against the minimum-distance engine per order type; skip a side if price is already through or within stops level of its level; raise buy-stop triggers by the spread so bid, not ask, must clear the level; attach server-side expiration (GTC else DAY/SPECIFIED per SYMBOL_EXPIRATION_MODE); modify an existing pending instead of duplicating; delete the opposite leg on fill; reserve margin for outstanding pendings.
features.rationale: Not needed if v1 enters at market on closed bars, but mandatory the moment any pending order is used: an orphaned straddle leg or a stale stop order is a real account risk. Server-side expiry (13509) protects when the terminal is offline, whereas OCO cancellation is client-side and can fail in exactly that case. Counting margin of existing pendings (17465) prevents a fill that the account cannot support. Stale-pending requoting within one tick (13233) is an HFT exchange technique and should not be carried over.
features.gold_silver_notes: Buy stops trigger on ask, so gold spread widening alone can fill a breakout order with no real move; the spread adjustment (1598) addresses this. Stop orders on gold fill with slippage through news and weekend gaps, so the fill must go through the same re-anchoring and risk check as market entries, and pending-based backtests should be trusted only after comparing with logged live fill slippage. On a hedging account a failed OCO leaves a locked long/short pair.

features.name: Execution-cost telemetry: stop slippage, fill slippage, real commission and swap
features.description: In OnTradeTransaction on DEAL_ADD: for exits with DEAL_REASON_SL compare deal price with DEAL_SL and log points filled worse than the stop; for entries log fill versus requested price and spread at send. Read commission and swap from deal history (HistorySelectByPosition) so every R figure is net of real costs. Persist the records and report distributions; feed observed slippage into tester assumptions and sizing.
features.rationale: Low count but high value for the stated goal of honest testability: it is the only mechanism in the category that measures how far live execution departs from the backtest. It is passive, has no parameters and cannot be curve-fitted. Reading costs from deals (74840) is preferable to inferring commission from one past trade (11449), which is fragile.
features.gold_silver_notes: Gold and silver stops slip most at news releases and across the weekend gap, while the tester generally fills stops at the stop price, so backtests understate loss per trade; the measured slippage distribution should be applied as a haircut to risk per trade. On raw-spread metal accounts commission is a material part of cost for short-horizon trades and must be inside every profit target and expectancy figure.

features.name: Virtual (hidden) SL/TP enforced by the EA instead of the server
features.description: An enum switches between broker-side SL/TP and hidden levels the EA enforces by sending a market close when floating points cross a threshold. The only defensible form is the hybrid the reader suggested: a hard server-side disaster SL is always present and sized against, and any tighter virtual level is treated as an extra exit rule, never as the protection.
features.rationale: As the stop mechanism it hides risk: there is no protection when the terminal, VPS or connection is down or the EA is throttled, and the tester closes virtual stops at the trigger tick with no latency, making the backtest more optimistic than live. It also contradicts the 'no position without a confirmed server-side stop' invariant. Single source of modest quality. If a virtual exit is ever added, risk must be sized on the server-side stop distance.
features.gold_silver_notes: Gold's fastest moves (news spikes, gaps at the reopen) are exactly when a client-side close arrives late or not at all, so a hidden stop on XAU/XAG can realise several times the planned loss. Stop-hunting concerns do not justify removing the server-side stop on an instrument this volatile.

features.name: Pending-to-market fallback and automatic order-type switching
features.description: When a stop order is rejected because price is already inside the minimum distance of its level, the wrapper converts it to a market order; trade panels likewise pick limit versus stop automatically by comparing the entry with bid/ask. An autonomous bot should instead skip that side and log the reason (gap-aware side skipping), keeping the order type fixed by the strategy.
features.rationale: It silently changes what the strategy is: a breakout stop becomes a late chase at market with a worse entry and smaller R, and a stop that turns into a limit inverts the trade logic from momentum to fade. Live behaviour then diverges from what was tested, and the divergence appears only in fast markets. Auto type selection is reasonable for a manual panel where a human chose the price, not for an automated entry.
features.gold_silver_notes: On gold the situation that triggers the fallback (price already at or through the level) is typically a spike or a gap, the worst moment to convert to a market order because spread and slippage are at their maximum.

features.name: Close-by netting and double-lot reversal (OrderCloseBy)
features.description: On hedging accounts, close a buy and a sell of the same magic against each other with close-by, or reverse by sending double lot the other way and closing the old ticket by the new one, paying one spread instead of two. Requires opposite positions to coexist and broker close-by support; unavailable on netting accounts.
features.rationale: It presupposes holding opposite positions at once, which a survival-first single-direction bot should never do, and the double-lot reversal briefly overshoots exposure and margin; if the second step fails the account is left with an unintended position. The benefit is one spread, the cost is account-mode dependence and an extra failure path. Both sources are MT4-era and low quality. A plain close followed by a normally gated new entry is safer and testable.
features.gold_silver_notes: The spread saved is small relative to a gold or silver trade's risk, while a failed second leg during a fast metals move leaves double or opposite exposure exactly when it is most expensive. Locked gold positions also accrue swap on both legs.

common_mistakes: Two-step entry (send naked, then attach SL/TP) without checking the modify result, without retries and without an emergency close, leaving positions unprotected (27964, 10925, 17373, 913, 17306).
Treating a broker-reported stops level or freeze level of 0 as 'no minimum distance'; ignoring the live spread and the freeze level entirely.

Applying a percentage safety multiplier to the stops level (x1.2, x1.5, x4) with no spread term, which stays 0 when the broker reports 0; or using tiny fixed fallbacks (5 or 10 points) that are below a normal gold spread.
Widening SL/TP to the broker minimum but not recomputing the lot size afterwards, so actual risk exceeds the intended risk (62732).
Applying the minimum-distance formula to absolute prices instead of distances (39402), or measuring stop distance from the wrong side of the quote (ask instead of bid for a long's SL/TP).
Normalising prices to _Digits only instead of SYMBOL_TRADE_TICK_SIZE, and comparing doubles for equality instead of using a half-tick tolerance.
Hard-coding the filling mode (FOK or IOC) and the order time type instead of deriving them from the symbol, so the EA never trades or cannot close on another broker.
Calling OrderCheck but sending the order anyway when it fails (49448), or not logging the check retcode and comment.
Applying margin/OrderCheck gates to closing or reducing orders, which can block an exit when margin is already short.
Retry loops with no attempt cap or no quote refresh (14833, 14869), and long Sleep calls inside the tick handler (up to 70 s in 11449) that freeze all other management.
Re-sending a failing entry on every tick of the entry window, or continuing to hammer the server after MARKET_CLOSED / TRADE_DISABLED with no backoff.
Trusting the boolean return of a trade call: clearing signal flags, counting a trade or counting an exit before the deal/position state was read back; ignoring partial fills.
Checking only PositionsTotal before entry, with no in-flight order guard, no timeout de-duplication and no restart-safe ownership scan, leading to duplicate positions.

Lot handling errors: rejecting instead of rounding to step (48251), silently clamping up to minimum lot when the risk-sized lot is smaller (62248), assuming two decimals of lot precision, and not announcing when traded size differs from requested size.

Using margin as the sizing basis (e.g. a fixed share of free margin) instead of only as a cap on a risk-sized lot; crude margin tests such as MODE_MARGINREQUIRED x lot against equity (14206) or a margin check that only runs on a tester dummy order (70900).

Hard-coded pip units and name-based metal detection, fixed pip thresholds (e.g. 2-pip trail step) and chart-symbol globals used while managing other symbols, all of which break across brokers, digits and price levels.

Per-tick trailing with no no-change check, no minimum improvement step, no freeze check and no throttle, producing modify spam and NO_CHANGES / TOO_MANY_REQUESTS errors; writing a freeze-level helper and never calling it (19963).

Hard-coded trading hours instead of the broker session table, no handling of sessions that wrap midnight, entries just before the daily break, and time exits scheduled at the close where they can be refused.
Acting on zero or stale quotes and on incomplete indicator buffers after reconnects or at session open.
Flatten routines that close positions before deleting pendings, iterate over a live list while closing, make a single pass with no leftover check, and never alert when they fail to get flat.

Pending orders with no server-side expiry and client-side-only OCO, buy stops not adjusted for spread, orders placed when price is already through the level, and no margin reserved for outstanding pendings.
Converting a rejected pending into a market order or auto-switching stop/limit type, which changes the strategy's semantics outside the backtest.
Relying on a static deviation value as slippage protection, with no pre-send price-drift check and no post-fill risk check.
Skipping trades silently: gates with no reason codes or logging, so differences between live and backtest behaviour cannot be diagnosed.
No measurement of realised stop slippage or real commission/swap, so backtest assumptions about gold and silver execution costs are never verified.

features.name: News blackout from the native MT5 economic calendar
features.description: On a 30-60 s timer call CalendarValueHistory over [now-after, now+before], resolve CalendarEventById and CalendarCountryById, and keep HIGH-importance events for an explicit currency map (XAU/XAG -> USD), optionally a keyword tier (NFP, CPI, FOMC) with wider windows. Cache a sorted array; per tick only compare times. Block new entries and pending placement only; management continues. Optional flag: cancel pendings or flatten once per event.
features.rationale: Scheduled USD releases are the most predictable source of spread blow-outs and stop slippage on metals, and the native calendar needs no WebRequest or DLL. The best examples (75652, 76605) cache the result and never block position management. Keep the windows fixed a priori (e.g. 30 min before / 30 min after for high impact) and do not optimise them. Flatten-before-news stays behind a flag because closing into a widening spread has its own cost. This is only honest if paired with the tester-compatible source in the next feature.
features.gold_silver_notes: Map XAUUSD/XAGUSD to USD explicitly: slicing the symbol into 3-letter halves fails on names like GOLD or XAUUSD.m, and XAU/XAG have no calendar events of their own. SYMBOL_CURRENCY_PROFIT (USD) is a safer automatic source than the name. Calendar times are in trade-server time. Silver follows gold on USD releases with larger percentage swings and a thinner book, so use the same or wider windows. A query limited to 'today' misses events just after server midnight; query a rolling window.

features.name: Tester-compatible news source: calendar CSV replay and date blacklist
features.description: Calendar functions are not available in the Strategy Tester. Export history once with a script (CalendarValueHistory to CSV: UTC time, currency, importance, name); when MQL_TESTER is set the EA loads it via FileOpen with FILE_COMMON and converts UTC to server time using the same rule-based offset as the session engine. Minimal fallback: a comma-separated date blacklist. Log loudly at init when no news source is active.
features.rationale: Without this the live bot runs a news filter that the backtest never exercised, so the tested system and the traded system differ. 76605 shows the CSV fallback with a GMT-to-server offset; 64444 shows the trivial date blacklist; 68215/58462/16308 show the cache-to-file pattern (their WebRequest scraping itself is unnecessary on MT5 and should not be in the trading EA). The minimum acceptable v1 is the explicit 'news filter inactive in this run' log line plus a blacklist of release dates.
features.gold_silver_notes: The set of USD releases that matters for metals is small (NFP, CPI, FOMC and similar), so a hand-checkable file covering the whole test span is realistic. The main bug class is time zones: store UTC in the file, and remember that TimeTradeServer()-TimeGMT() is zero in the tester, so the offset must come from the DST rule engine, not auto-detection.

features.name: News straddle / event breakout trading (OCO stops around releases)
features.description: Place a BuyStop and SellStop either side of price shortly before a release, cancel the opposite leg on fill, then trail aggressively, sometimes with a separate news-risk budget. Only the plumbing is worth keeping: server-side pending expiration (ORDER_TIME_SPECIFIED) so nothing lingers if the terminal dies, and once-per-event action flags.
features.rationale: A backtest of a straddle around a release is not trustworthy: the tester does not reproduce the spread widening, stop-order slippage and partial liquidity of the release second, so the result measures the tester's fill model rather than an edge. It also adds a second strategy with its own risk budget to a bot whose first goal is survival. Seen only in quality 2-3 EAs. The news calendar should be used to stand aside, not to trade.
features.gold_silver_notes: On gold the release spike often triggers both legs (whipsaw) and the stop order fills well beyond its price; silver is worse because its spread is larger relative to price. 11003 is listed by its title (a news straddle EA); the idea extracted from it was only its pre-placement spread cap, which belongs to the spread gate feature.

features.name: Cost-relative spread gate with hard cap, entry-only
features.description: At order placement measure spread as Ask-Bid from SymbolInfoTick, not SYMBOL_SPREAD. Reject when spread exceeds a set fraction of the stop distance (10-15% in the best examples; 'SL >= 3x spread' is the loose variant) or TP is under ~3x spread, adding round-trip commission converted to price. Keep one absolute backstop cap in price or tick-size multiples. Apply to entries, pending placement and discretionary exits only; protective stops stay server-side.
features.rationale: The most consistently good idea in the category and present in the highest-quality EAs (77691, 78259, 77639, 78778). Expressing cost as a fraction of the trade's own risk unit is scale-free, tightens automatically when the stop is small, and needs no per-symbol tuning, unlike the fixed point caps of older EAs. One parameter, chosen a priori. It must never block protective exits, and every veto must be logged.
features.gold_silver_notes: Works unchanged across 2- and 3-digit gold quotes and on silver. Silver's spread is larger relative to its price and ATR, so the same ratio will veto more short-stop trades there; that is correct information, not a defect. In the tester the gate is only meaningful with 'every tick based on real ticks'; generated ticks use the bar's recorded or a fixed spread and will understate vetoes.

features.name: Empirical execution-cost baseline (spread and slippage recorder) and adaptive cap
features.description: Separate recorder tool: weight each spread value by the milliseconds it stood until the next tick, aggregate into 24 server-hour and session buckets (average, average-of-max, max) plus daily min/max, and log fill slippage from OnTradeTransaction. Use the tables offline to set the fixed limits of the spread gate and blackout windows. Optional live variant: cap = k x that hour's normal spread, or pause when recent slippage degrades.
features.rationale: As a measurement tool it is low-risk and valuable: it replaces guessed thresholds with broker-specific data (79460 is quality 5). As a live adaptive gate it adds state, depends on tick feed, and can normalise bad conditions (k x 'normal rollover spread' accepts a spread that should be refused). So: run the recorder alongside v1, keep the gate thresholds fixed, and put any adaptive cap or slippage-based pause behind a flag later. Session-scaled caps (69651) add tunable multipliers for little gain.
features.gold_silver_notes: Metal spreads have a strong intraday shape: tightest in the London/New York overlap, widest around the daily break and at the weekly open. Record per broker and per symbol; silver needs its own table. A 30-tick rolling average (11449) spans very different time lengths in quiet versus fast gold markets, so prefer time-weighted statistics.

features.name: Tradability gate: broker session table, pre-close margin, rollover blackout, stale-quote check
features.description: Before any order work read SymbolInfoSessionTrade for the current weekday (every session index, including sessions wrapping midnight) and require an open session that does not end within N minutes. Add a configurable rollover blackout (e.g. 10 min before to 60 min after the daily break) and require the last tick's time_msc to be younger than N seconds. Gates entries and stop modifications, never emergency closes.
features.rationale: Pure hygiene with no fitted parameters: it removes 'market closed' rejections, orders sent into the daily break, and decisions taken on a frozen price. Reading the broker's own table (77691, 78891, 61921, 17465) is more robust than hard-coded hours such as 'skip server hour 0' (69651), which is wrong on any broker with a different offset. The stale-quote test (79460, 15708) is one comparison per tick.
features.gold_silver_notes: Gold and silver have a daily break of about an hour (typically around 17:00-18:00 New York) and broker-specific hours that differ from FX. Spreads blow out just before and after the break, so the blackout should be wider than the break itself. Holiday-shortened sessions are not always reflected in the session table, which is another reason to keep the stale-quote check.

features.name: Entry time window with midnight wrap (minute resolution, per weekday)
features.description: Work in minute-of-day: allowed = start<=end ? (t>=start && t<end) : (t>=start || t<end); define equal start/end explicitly as 'filter off'. Optionally several windows per weekday, parsed and validated once in OnInit from 'HH:MM-HH:MM;HH:MM-HH:MM' strings. The window gates new entries only; trailing and exits keep running outside it. Choose one or two windows a priori rather than optimising hour by hour.
features.rationale: The most common filter in the set and trivial to get right, but most implementations are hour-only, server-time-only, or mishandle start > end. It belongs in v1 as plain plumbing. The risk is not the code but the use: optimising start/end hours is a classic curve fit, so windows should come from market structure (London, New York) and be fed by the DST-aware engine. Per-weekday strings are flexible but multiply the parameters; keep them fixed.
features.gold_silver_notes: Gold and silver liquidity concentrates in London and the London/New York overlap; Asia is thinner with wider spreads. Raw server-time windows drift by an hour twice a year relative to those sessions unless converted. Keep the rollover hour outside every window.

features.name: DST-aware session anchoring and rule-based server offset
features.description: Define sessions in market-local time (London, New York) and convert to server time with deterministic rules: US DST from the 2nd Sunday of March to the 1st Sunday of November, UK/EU DST between the last Sundays of March and October, plus a broker profile input (fixed GMT, EU-DST, NY-close). Use TimeTradeServer()-TimeGMT() only as a live cross-check. The same routine sets the trading-day boundary. Unit-test transition dates.
features.rationale: Required for honest testing of any session-based logic: without it a 'London open' rule is an hour off for part of every year, and backtest and live disagree. The quality 4-5 examples (78259, 17465, 68082) compute DST by rule; the auto-detect and TimeGMT approaches (79460, 77180, 76605) are fine live but collapse in the tester, where TimeGMT equals server time. 78702 shows the same offset logic reused for a configurable day boundary with self-tests, which is the right standard.
features.gold_silver_notes: US and UK/EU clocks change on different dates, so for a few weeks each spring and autumn London and New York sessions shift relative to each other. Many metals brokers run a server clock that follows the New York close (server midnight = 17:00 New York), giving five clean D1 bars a week; GMT+0 servers produce Sunday stub bars that distort D1 ATR and day-based filters.

features.name: Scheduled flatten and week-edge guards (Friday cutoff, weekly-open wait, daily flat time)
features.description: Block new entries after a Friday cutoff and for N minutes after the weekly open, both derived from the symbol's session table rather than fixed hours. Optional scheduler closes positions and deletes pendings at a set time before the daily break, firing exactly once per day via a persisted date key and retrying until confirmed flat. Holding overnight or over weekends is a declared strategy property.
features.rationale: A stop-loss does not protect across a gap, so not opening fresh risk into the weekend and not trading the first minutes of the weekly open are cheap survival rules with no fitted edge. The daily flat time depends on strategy style (intraday yes, H4 swing no), so it is an input, but the scheduler must exist and be exactly-once (78968) rather than 'if hour > 18 close' on every tick (8595). Monday-skip toggles (7612, 18704) are day-of-week fitting and should not be optimised.
features.gold_silver_notes: Weekend gaps in gold can exceed a normal stop distance and silver gaps are proportionally larger. Swap on metals is material for multi-day holds. Schedule the flat time ahead of the pre-close margin (17465 flattens about 31 minutes before session end) so the close is not executed inside the rollover spread spike.

features.name: Setup-geometry sanity band normalised by ATR
features.description: Before sending a trade require the structural stop or setup range to sit inside a band of one closed-bar volatility unit: stop at least ~0.5x ATR of the signal timeframe, range within min/max fractions of D1 ATR(14) (0.15-0.70 seen for a session range), stop no wider than k x ATR(H1), and above SYMBOL_TRADE_STOPS_LEVEL. Otherwise skip and mark the setup done for the day.
features.rationale: This is a validity check on the trade rather than a predictive filter: a stop inside the noise or a range several times normal makes the risk unit meaningless and distorts position sizing. The good examples (75586, 77639, 77094, 78293) all normalise by ATR; the older ones (18704, 21452) use fixed points and are not portable. Keep the band wide and fixed. A plain ATR is enough for v1; blended ADR (24786) or MA-smoothed ATR (11739) are refinements, and the range-derived step with clamps (11585, 12872) came from grid spacing and is not adopted for that purpose.
features.gold_silver_notes: Gold's price level changes several-fold over a long test span, so any threshold in points or dollars is wrong for most of the history; ATR fractions stay comparable. Silver has higher percentage volatility, so the same ATR-relative band applies but absolute stops are very different. Build D1 ATR on clean daily bars (no Sunday stubs).

features.name: Closed-bar volatility shock pause (ATR ratio / bar range versus ATR)
features.description: On each new bar compute short ATR / long ATR from closed bars (ATR(5)/ATR(20) or ATR(20)/ATR(100)); when the ratio exceeds a ceiling (about 1.5), or the last bar's range or percent move is abnormal versus ATR, block new entries for a cooldown of N bars. An optional floor skips dead markets. Ratio-based, so one setting carries across price levels; calendar-free and reproducible in the tester.
features.rationale: The calendar only covers scheduled events; this is the one shock guard that also catches unscheduled moves and behaves identically in backtest and live. Use it as a circuit breaker with one conservative ceiling fixed a priori, kept out of the optimiser and compared against a no-filter run. Caveats: for breakout entries expansion is the signal, so apply only an extreme ceiling there; the floor, volume ratios and session-specific multipliers (69651), the +/-61.8% blended band (17465) and the indicator-based volatmeter (9499) add parameters and should stay off in v1. In 62684 it gated grid adds, which does not make a grid safe.
features.gold_silver_notes: Gold moves on unscheduled headlines as well as on data, so a calendar-only filter leaves a gap. Fixed thresholds such as a 0.24% one-bar move (1480) or ATR floors in points (69651) do not transfer between gold and silver or across years; use ratios to the instrument's own ATR. Silver's spikes are larger relative to its baseline, so expect more pauses at the same ceiling.

features.name: Tick-velocity fast-market detector with cooldown
features.description: Measure mid-price change per second between ticks (or per timer poll), optionally scaled by recent M1 tick volume; above a threshold set a flag that blocks first entries for N minutes. Implement with time_msc deltas, a minimum time base to avoid division spikes on near-simultaneous ticks, and thresholds expressed as ATR fractions rather than points.
features.rationale: Reacts faster than any closed-bar filter, but its behaviour depends on the broker's tick feed and on the tester's tick model, so it is not reproducible without real-tick data and is easy to tune to one feed. Its best-known example (76605) is a recovery EA where it also widens grid spacing, i.e. it was compensating for risky money management. If used, start in log-only mode and compare flags against the closed-bar shock pause before letting it gate trades.
features.gold_silver_notes: Gold tick rates jump at releases and brokers aggregate ticks differently, so a points-per-second threshold calibrated on one feed will misfire on another. Tick volume on OTC metals is broker-specific, which weakens the volume-scaled variant (24786).

features.name: Compression/expansion day filters (NR4/NR7, yesterday range versus ADR, Bollinger width)
features.description: Classify the prior closed D1 bar (Sunday stub bars dropped) as contracted or expanded: narrowest of 4/7, inside day plus NR4, range as a percent of the N-day mean range (25-150% seen), or normalised band width (upper-lower)/middle. Breakout logic trades after contraction; mean-reversion stands aside after blow-off days. Always keep FILTER_NONE as the control and express thresholds as ratios, never points.
features.rationale: A legitimate, published idea, and 78259 (quality 5) implements it properly with a control group. But it is a predictive regime filter with many variants and thresholds, it cuts the trade count sharply, and choosing the variant after seeing results is curve fitting. Add it only after the unfiltered v1 is characterised, one variant at a time. The Bollinger-width versions (11472, 25848, 16350) use fixed point widths and are redundant with an ATR-relative measure; the fixed 150-point previous-day kill (8417) is unusable as written.
features.gold_silver_notes: The NR filters were applied to a gold opening-range breakout in 78259. Gold's wide and narrow days cluster around the macro calendar, so these filters partly duplicate the news blackout. D1 bars must be built on a consistent day boundary; stub bars make 'narrowest of 4' meaningless.

features.name: Higher-timeframe trend/regime agreement gate
features.description: One simple direction filter read from the last closed higher-timeframe bar: price versus an EMA (or EMA50 > EMA200), optionally ADX above a level with +DI/-DI for direction; trade only with it and stand aside when neutral. Create handles once in OnInit, read shift 1 with CopyBuffer, and expose a mode input (none/EMA/ADX/both) so its contribution is measured against the unfiltered strategy.
features.rationale: Direction bias is part of the strategy definition, not of the protective filter layer, and each variant (EMA stack, ADX/DI, SuperTrend, Alligator, DEMA slope) brings periods and thresholds to tune. If the entry logic needs a bias, pick the simplest one a priori and keep the 'none' mode for comparison. The four-state ADX switch that routes between trend and mean-reversion strategies (9499) doubles the system to be validated and is not for v1. 74894 applied the gate only to add-on entries; it should cover all entries or none.
features.gold_silver_notes: Gold has had long one-directional stretches, so a trend filter fitted on such a sample may simply encode a long bias; check long and short results separately and across sub-periods. Silver trends less cleanly and whipsaws more, so a filter that helps gold should not be assumed to help silver.

features.name: Over-extension filter (distance from baseline in ATR)
features.description: Skip a trend or breakout entry when the last closed price is more than k x ATR (about 1) beyond the baseline/mean or beyond the broken level, so the bot does not chase an exhausted move; optionally require a minimum penetration to avoid entering too early. Distance must be ATR-normalised and computed on the closed bar.
features.rationale: A reasonable entry-quality rule that also keeps the stop distance sane, but it is one more threshold and it removes exactly the strongest momentum trades, so its net effect is strategy-specific and must be shown against a control. 74840 uses a raw distance in points and adds a slope requirement; 71645 bundles it with ATR-expansion, price-velocity and tick-volume scores, which is a stack of fitted thresholds. Only the single ATR-distance form (28117) is worth carrying.
features.gold_silver_notes: Gold can stay extended from its mean for long periods in a trend, so a tight k cuts the best runs. Tick-volume confirmation (71645) is unreliable on OTC metals because tick volume is broker-specific.

features.name: Attempt limiter: one attempt per day/window plus entry cooldown, persisted
features.description: Key each attempt by trading day (year*1000 + day_of_year of the session day), optionally by direction or window, and store the key when the signal is evaluated whether or not a trade results. Add a minimum seconds/bars cooldown between entries. Persist in terminal GlobalVariables and rebuild in OnInit from HistorySelect deals and open positions filtered by magic number, never from in-memory flags alone.
features.rationale: Caps how much damage a bad day or a signal loop can do and makes trade counts predictable, with no fitted edge. Almost every example keeps the latch in memory (214, 68125, 18704), so a restart or VPS reboot re-arms it and the bot trades the same setup twice; persistence and reconstruction from trade history are the actual feature. Cooldowns should be in seconds or bars of a named timeframe, not PeriodSeconds of whatever chart the EA sits on (22705).
features.gold_silver_notes: Gold's London and New York bursts invite immediate re-entry after a stop-out, which is where scalpers bleed. The day key must follow the same trading-day boundary as the session engine (not 'hour 0' on an arbitrary server clock). Apply the limit per symbol; gold and silver move together, so a daily attempt on each is close to two attempts on one idea.

features.name: Gate pipeline with reason codes, veto logging and per-filter switches
features.description: Route every filter through one function returning an enum reason (SPREAD, NEWS, SESSION, ROLLOVER, VOL_SHOCK, ...). Log each vetoed signal once per bar with the measured value and its threshold, count vetoes per reason, and report the counts on the panel, in OnDeinit and from OnTester. Each filter has its own on/off input so it can be compared against a no-filter control run.
features.rationale: This is what makes the other filters honestly testable. Logged vetoes (77060) let live and backtest be reconciled trade by trade; a visible block reason (72527, 78778, 11449) explains why the bot is idle; a FILTER_NONE control (78259) shows whether a filter adds anything or just removes trades. Without it, filters accumulate silently and nobody can tell which one produced the equity curve.
features.gold_silver_notes: On metals the spread, rollover and news vetoes will dominate the counts. Comparing veto counts by hour between a real-tick backtest and live trading is the quickest check that the tester's spread model matches the broker's actual gold and silver spreads.

features.name: Self-calibrating and pseudo-statistical filters
features.description: Gates derived from in-loop re-optimisation or thin statistics: allow only the side whose simulated trades did better over a recent lookback, a drift-to-noise ratio |mean/std| of the last 20 log returns, or a value-area/POC built from a histogram of bar closes and refreshed every few minutes.
