features.rationale: Each looks rigorous but rests on too little data or on re-fitting inside the bot. A direction switch based on which side recently simulated better (19392) is performance chasing with hidden parameters and cannot be validated out of sample because it keeps changing. Twenty returns give a drift estimate that is mostly noise (73622). A POC from close counts without real volume (62713) is not a volume profile; its own reader noted it would need real volume to mean anything. All come from quality 2-3 EAs and all add opaque state that makes test results hard to interpret.
features.gold_silver_notes: Spot gold and silver are OTC at retail brokers, so there is no true volume and tick volume differs by broker; any profile or volume-derived statistic is feed-specific. Gold regime shifts are driven by macro news, which a 20-bar statistic cannot anticipate.

common_mistakes: Thresholds in fixed points or pips (max spread, range width, band width, previous-day range, one-bar move). They do not transfer between gold and silver, between 2- and 3-digit quotes, or across years in which gold's price level changed several-fold; use fractions of ATR or of the trade's own stop distance.
Session hours hard-coded in raw server time with no DST handling, so 'London open' or 'New York open' is an hour off for part of every year and differs between brokers.

Deriving the server offset from TimeTradeServer()-TimeGMT() or building windows on TimeGMT. This works live but in the Strategy Tester TimeGMT equals server time, so the backtest runs different hours from live.

Relying on the MT5 calendar for a news filter without a tester source. Calendar functions are unavailable in the Strategy Tester, so the filter is silently inactive in every backtest and the tested bot is not the traded bot.

Detecting news currencies by slicing the symbol name into 3-letter halves or by substring match. This fails on GOLD, suffixed symbols and XAU/XAG (which have no events); metals need an explicit map to USD.
Fetching third-party calendar pages with WebRequest inside the trading EA: trading blocks on the network, the feed's time zone is easy to misread, and the result cannot be backtested.
Reading SYMBOL_SPREAD / MODE_SPREAD or a single tick sample instead of measuring Ask-Bid at the moment of order placement, and ignoring commission in the cost check.
Applying spread or session gates to exits and protective logic, or pairing a spread-gated soft exit with no server-side stop. Filters should block new risk, never the ability to get out.

Time-window code that breaks when start > end (midnight wrap), has hour-only resolution, or leaves equal start/end undefined; hard-coding 'hour 0' as rollover or a Friday hour regardless of the broker's clock.

One-trade-per-day and per-window latches kept only in memory and reset at server hour 0. A restart re-arms them and the bot repeats the trade; state must be persisted and rebuilt from positions and deal history.

Stacking many thresholded regime filters (ATR floors and ceilings, band width, ADX, volume ratios, distance bands, day-of-week skips) without a no-filter control. Each adds parameters, shrinks the sample and makes the backtest a fit.

Using volatility or news filters to make grid, martingale or recovery sizing look safe (several source EAs gate grid adds this way). A filter reduces how often the tail is hit; it does not remove the tail.

Tick-based detectors (tick velocity, tick speed, N-tick spread averages) and tick-volume filters treated as if they were portable. They depend on the broker's feed and the tester's tick model, and tick volume on OTC metals is not real volume.
Silent vetoes: skipped trades are not logged with a reason, so live and backtest results cannot be reconciled and nobody knows which filter is doing the work.
Evaluating filters on the forming bar or on indicators that repaint, and creating indicator handles repeatedly instead of once in OnInit with closed-bar reads.
Flatten logic that fires on every tick while a condition holds, or that closes positions inside the rollover or pre-news spread spike, instead of once per event and ahead of the widening.
Day-based filters computed on D1 bars that include Sunday stub bars or an inconsistent day boundary, which corrupts ATR, NR4/NR7 and previous-day range tests.
Querying the calendar only for 'today', which misses events shortly after server midnight, or refreshing it either every tick (slow) or once a day (stale, misses revised times).
Trading the news with stop-order straddles and trusting the backtest, which does not model release-time spread widening and slippage.
Testing spread-sensitive rules on generated ticks or a fixed tester spread; spread gates and cost ratios are only meaningful on real-tick data.

features.name: Position-level trade journal rebuilt from deals (net of all costs)
features.description: On each close (OnTradeTransaction DEAL_ADD) and at OnDeinit/OnTester, HistorySelect and walk deals chronologically, grouped by DEAL_POSITION_ID and filtered by magic and symbol. Sum profit, commission, swap and fee over all deals; handle partial closes and DEAL_ENTRY_INOUT reversals with pro-rata commission; emit one row only when open volume returns to zero. Same code in tester and live.
features.rationale: Every other statistic depends on a correct per-position net result. Entry-deal commission and swap are the costs most often dropped, which flatters win rate and expectancy. Running the identical journal in the tester and live is what makes backtest-versus-live reconciliation possible. The weaker variants (77094, 77220) only notice a vanished ticket and keep a running win rate; the 79024 deal-loop version is the one to copy.
features.gold_silver_notes: Metals swaps are large and include a triple-swap day, and commission per lot differs a lot between brokers, so gross P/L is misleading for multi-day gold holds. Money results are not comparable between XAUUSD and XAGUSD (typical contract 100 oz vs 5000 oz) or across years in which the gold price multiplied, so also store P/L in basis points of price using traded volume (77060).

features.name: R-multiple against the initial stop, plus MFE/MAE per trade
features.description: Read the initial stop from the opening order (HistoryOrderGetDouble ORDER_SL) or store it at entry. Risk money = OrderCalcProfit from entry to that stop; R = net P/L including commission and swap divided by it, never against a trailed stop. MFE/MAE from M1 highs/lows between entry and exit (CopyRates), exported in points, money and R. Also report P/L in basis points of price.
features.rationale: R against the original stop is the only unit that stays comparable across lot sizes, volatility regimes and price levels, and it exposes whether trailing or breakeven logic actually adds anything. MFE/MAE shows whether stops are too tight or targets unreachable. The risk is tuning SL/TP to the excursion distribution of the same sample, so treat it as a diagnostic and confirm any change on unseen data.
features.gold_silver_notes: Point distances are not stable on gold (the same 500 points is a very different fraction of price and ATR in different years), so analyse excursions in R or bps, not points. M1 highs/lows are bid prices: for shorts add the spread to the adverse excursion, which matters on silver and during spread spikes. Excursions measured on the entry and exit bars include price action outside the holding period, so they are slightly overstated.

features.name: Session, weekday, hour and exit-reason tags with bucket tables
features.description: Tag every journal row with entry hour in UTC (server time minus an explicit offset), session (Asia/London/NY), weekday, setup type and the exit DEAL_REASON (SL, TP, EXPERT, CLIENT, SO). At OnDeinit/OnTester print per-bucket trade count, expectancy in R, worst floating loss and total profit. Always print the count beside each average so thin buckets are visible.
features.rationale: Tagging is cheap and makes results explainable: where the losses come from, how many exits were stop-outs, whether one session carries the whole result. The danger is the next step: building hour or weekday filters out of the same backtest table is plain data mining. Keep the tags in v1, but only accept a session filter that has a structural reason and survives out of sample. In the tester TimeGMT equals simulated server time, so the UTC offset must be an explicit input.
features.gold_silver_notes: Directly useful for metals: behaviour and cost differ sharply between Asia, the London open, the New York open and the daily maintenance break around 17:00 New York, where spreads blow out. Broker server time and DST differ between brokers, so tag in UTC or results will not transfer. Silver is thinner in Asia, so its hour buckets will be smaller and noisier than gold's; do not copy a gold hour filter onto silver without its own evidence.

features.name: Execution-cost telemetry: signed slippage, fill latency and spread
features.description: Per deal: slippage = (requested - filled)/point for buys, reversed for sells, positive = favourable. Requested price is the SL/TP level for stop/target exits, else ORDER_PRICE_OPEN, else the last bid/ask from CopyTicks in the 60 s before ORDER_TIME_SETUP_MSC. Latency = DEAL_TIME_MSC - ORDER_TIME_SETUP_MSC. Keep running mean and max by exit reason and hour; log spread at send. A companion recorder tabulates current/min/max spread per symbol.
features.rationale: Most of the gap between a backtest and a live account is execution cost, and it cannot be assumed, only measured. These numbers are what justify the spread, slippage and delay settings used in the tester. Nothing here can be curve-fitted. The MQL4-style variants (GetTickCount around OrderSend, slippage against the price the EA sent) miss stop exits, which is where slippage is worst. In v1 only record; do not let the bot adapt its behaviour to these numbers yet.
features.gold_silver_notes: Stop-loss slippage on XAUUSD around NFP, CPI, FOMC and at session reopen can be many times the normal spread, and 77060 warns that M1 bar spread understates the real reopen spread by roughly 3x, so test on real ticks. Silver spread as a fraction of price is much wider than gold's. Use the multi-symbol spread table to compare the broker's symbol variants (XAUUSD, suffixed versions, XAGUSD) by hour before choosing what and when to trade. Express slippage in bps or R as well as points.

features.name: Decision journal with reason codes and a single order-send choke point
features.description: Every evaluated signal produces one line: bar time, key filter values, position state and an enumerated outcome (ENTER, or SKIP with reason: spread X > Y, session, daily cap, margin, position open). All OrderSend/OrderCheck calls go through one wrapper that logs the request, quote, broker constraints (stops level, tick size, volume specs), retcode with text, order/deal ticket and fill price. The core line cannot be disabled.
features.rationale: This is what makes the bot honestly testable: a backtest and a live run can be compared decision by decision, and a missing trade always has a stated cause. A single send wrapper is also the natural place for pre-trade validation and retcode handling. Count skips per reason at deinit so a filter that silently blocks most signals is visible. Do not carry telemetry in the order comment (15708): brokers truncate or overwrite it.
features.gold_silver_notes: On metals most missed or rejected trades come from spread spikes, the stops/freeze level, the daily break (market closed) and off-quotes or requotes around news. Logging the spread, stops level and quote at send time explains them without guesswork. The skip-reason counts also show how often the spread filter fires on silver, which tells you whether the filter threshold is realistic for that broker.

features.name: Risk audit: sizing line, planned-versus-realised loss, never-widen-stop check
features.description: At entry log balance, risk money, stop distance, loss per lot (OrderCalcProfit), lots after step rounding and expected loss at stop; store planned risk and equity. On DEAL_ENTRY_OUT in OnTradeTransaction log realised net loss against planned risk and their ratio. In tester/OnDeinit scan each closed position's order history and flag any SL later moved further from price than the first one. Violations count as test failures.
features.rationale: Sizing errors are the most common way an EA destroys an account, and they are invisible unless every input to the lot calculation is printed. The realised/planned ratio turns gap and slippage risk into a measured number instead of an assumption. The stop-widening scan is a cheap invariant: a survival-first bot must never loosen a stop, and this proves it on every test run.
features.gold_silver_notes: Tick value, tick size, digits and contract size for XAUUSD and XAGUSD differ between brokers, so any hard-coded pip value is wrong somewhere; OrderCalcProfit plus the audit line catches it on the first trade. Weekend and news gaps make realised loss exceed planned loss, more so on silver; watch the tail of the realised/planned ratio, not its average. On small accounts check that minimum lot does not already exceed the risk budget.

features.name: Logging plumbing: levels, change-based throttling, durable append-only CSV
features.description: One Log(level, code, text) wrapper with ERR/WARN/INFO/DBG threshold. Repeats are suppressed by printing only when the reason or retcode changes, or at most once per bar/60 s; errors and trade events are never throttled. CSV sink: FILE_READ|FILE_WRITE|FILE_SHARE_READ, header only when empty, seek to end, FileFlush per row, buffer rows while locked, resume after the last written row. Rows carry equity, balance, drawdown, daily P/L.
features.rationale: The journals above are only useful if they are readable and survive restarts, crashes and a spreadsheet holding the file open. Change-based suppression keeps a condition that blocks trading tick after tick from flooding the log while losing no information. Avoid the 56773 variant that prints only every 500th message in the tester: it drops events arbitrarily and makes tester logs differ from live logs. Name files by symbol and magic so instances never share a file.
features.gold_silver_notes: Gold ticks very fast during news; a tick-level block such as 'spread above maximum' can otherwise write thousands of identical lines a minute, exactly when the log matters most. Separate files per symbol keep the XAUUSD and XAGUSD instances from interleaving or locking each other. An account snapshot on every event row lets you see equity at the moment of a news spike rather than only at trade close.

features.name: Tester and optimiser hygiene: strict input validation, no UI in tester
features.description: OnInit checks every input and cross-constraint (trailing step <= trailing start < take profit, positive stops, risk caps, symbol exists via SymbolExist including suffix) and returns INIT_PARAMETERS_INCORRECT instead of silently defaulting, so the optimiser drops the pass. Panels, chart objects, Comment and sleeps run only when not in tester/optimisation or when MQL_VISUAL_MODE is set. Trading logic stays identical in tester and live.
features.rationale: Silent defaulting means the test ran with parameters other than the ones shown, which is dishonest by construction. Rejecting nonsense combinations in OnInit is cleaner than returning early from OnTick (31582), which leaves zero-trade passes in the result table. Skipping UI only affects speed. The one rule to hold: tester-specific branches may skip drawing, sleeping and notifications, never anything that changes orders.
features.gold_silver_notes: Metal symbol names vary by broker (plain, suffixed, or named differently), so fail loudly when the configured symbol is missing rather than trading the chart symbol by accident. Validate stop and target distances against the symbol's stops level at init, since metals often have a non-zero stops level that makes tight scalping parameters untradeable live even though the tester accepts them.

features.name: OnTester criterion with hard gates and early/late consistency
features.description: In OnTester rebuild closed-position results from deal history, split them by time (e.g. 70/30) and compute profit factor, recovery factor and payoff per segment. Reject (return a strongly negative value) passes with too few trades in either segment, a losing segment or late-segment recovery factor below 1. Otherwise return a sign-preserving risk-adjusted score, e.g. Sharpe times |profit|, scaled by early-versus-late consistency ratios.
features.rationale: Left alone, the optimiser ranks by balance, which is the strongest invitation to curve fitting. Minimum-trade and no-losing-segment gates remove lucky low-sample passes; the sign-preserving form keeps losing passes ranked below zero. The limit must be stated plainly: the optimiser still selects on the late segment, so it is a consistency filter, not a holdout. Keep a separate untouched forward period and demo run. Source 63193 is low-quality code; take the idea, not the implementation, and set the trade-count gate well above its 20.
features.gold_silver_notes: Gold has had multi-year one-directional regimes, so a 70/30 time split can put both segments inside the same rally and pass a strategy that is only long beta. Add gates on long and short results separately, or on several calendar sub-periods, before trusting the score. Silver produces fewer clean signals, so the trade-count gate will reject more passes; that is the correct outcome, not a reason to lower the gate.

features.name: Cost-aware expectancy checks: breakeven win rate and pessimistic bar resolution
features.description: Per trade compute breakeven win rate risk/(risk+reward) and its net version (risk+cost)/(risk+reward); print the averages beside the achieved win rate in reports and entry alerts. In any bar-based replay, a bar that straddles both stop and target counts as a stop, and recorded spread plus slippage are charged both ways against the result rather than by shifting the entry. Report expectancy, profit factor and drawdown in R.
features.rationale: Showing the required win rate next to the achieved one is trivial to compute and immediately exposes setups whose high win rate comes only from a near target. The stop-first rule and charging costs on both sides are the conservative assumptions any internal simulation must use. What should stay out of v1 is the source EA's use of the replay to rank parameter combinations on the live chart: that is a hidden self-optimiser. Keep the report and the assumptions, not the live combo selection.
features.gold_silver_notes: For gold scalping the spread plus slippage is a large share of the stop distance, so the net breakeven win rate can sit far above the gross one; silver is worse because its cost is a bigger fraction of a typical stop. Wide news bars on metals regularly contain both stop and target, so the stop-first rule changes results materially. Anything with stops of only a few spreads must be verified on real ticks, not bar replay.

features.name: Random-entry benchmark mode (null hypothesis)
features.description: A tester-only input replaces the entry signal with a seeded coin flip (MathSrand, MathRand) at a comparable entry frequency, leaving stop, target, sizing, breakeven, filters and cost model untouched. Run many seeds to obtain a distribution of results; the real signal must clearly beat that distribution, not a single run. OnInit refuses this mode outside the Strategy Tester.
features.rationale: It answers the question a backtest alone cannot: how much of the result comes from the signal and how much from exit geometry, risk engine and market drift. It costs one input and a few lines, and it cannot be over-fitted because it has nothing to tune. A single random run proves nothing either way, so compare against a spread of seeds. The live-account guard is mandatory.
features.gold_silver_notes: Gold's long upward drift makes random long entries with a trailing stop look profitable over many test windows. Give the benchmark the same long/short mix and the same trading hours as the real strategy, otherwise the comparison is contaminated by drift and session effects. If the real signal on XAUUSD cannot beat random entries with the same exits, the edge is the trend of the sample, not the strategy.

features.name: Built-in self-tests: known-answer checks and state round trip
features.description: A RunSelfTest() routine (input flag or tester start) exercises pure helpers such as lot sizing, price and volume normalisation, slippage sign and parsers with known answers, including must-not-match cases. A persistence round trip saves non-default state, wipes variables, reloads and compares every field. Logging code replays synthetic ticks and asserts the rows. Results are written OK/FAILED to a file; any failure fails OnInit.
features.rationale: MQL5 has no test framework, so the practical route is to keep risk and state logic in pure functions and ship the tests inside the EA. This catches regressions in exactly the code that protects the account (sizing, daily-loss state, restart recovery) before any market data is involved. It appears only in the highest-quality sources (78748, 79035, 79460), which is a signal in itself.
features.gold_silver_notes: Include test cases built from metal specifications: different digits and tick sizes for gold and silver, contract sizes of 100 oz and 5000 oz, volume step and minimum lot, and suffixed symbol names. Test the daily-loss state across the day rollover and the daily break, since that boundary is where a reset bug would re-enable trading after a loss limit was hit.

features.name: Timer-driven, rate-limited notifications and heartbeat
features.description: Alerts enter a bounded queue; OnTimer merges and sends at most one push (255 chars, 'first + N more') and one web message per ~10 s. Nothing is sent from OnTick or OnTradeTransaction. A heartbeat (balance, equity, margin level, positions) goes out on a fixed interval and immediately when PositionsTotal changes. Each channel is switchable, repeats are capped with a minimum gap, all off in tester.
features.rationale: Useful for supervision but not part of survival logic, and it adds external dependencies (push limits, WebRequest allow-list, third-party endpoints). If added, the 78748 design is the only safe one: network calls block, so they must never sit in a trade path, and push limits make unbatched alerts fail exactly during bursts. Keep it one-way telemetry; a remote command channel is a different and riskier feature. DLL-based transports (1246) should not be used.
features.gold_silver_notes: The events worth a notification on metals are halts and anomalies: daily-loss lock, stop-out, repeated rejections, abnormal slippage after news. News bursts generate many events in seconds, which is why merging matters. A tick-based liveness alarm would fire falsely during the daily break and the weekend, so drive the heartbeat from the timer and report market-closed as a state rather than a fault.

features.name: Trade-list robustness analytics: bootstrap Monte Carlo, distribution metrics, per-pass frames
features.description: From the closed-position list compute SQN, Ulcer index, Sortino, Calmar, skewness, kurtosis, maximum consecutive losses and separate long/short statistics. Bootstrap about 1000 resamples with replacement of net trade results; report median ending equity, median maximum drawdown and the share of runs touching a ruin level. During optimisation, send the balance curve and statistics per pass with FrameAdd and read them in OnTesterPass.
features.rationale: It replaces the single backtest drawdown with a distribution, which is more honest, and frames let you inspect the whole population of passes instead of the top row. But resampling trades independently destroys loss clustering, so the drawdown and ruin figures are optimistic and must be read as a lower bound. The Kelly fraction from a backtest must never feed position sizing. It can all be done offline from the core CSV journal, so it does not need to be in v1.
features.gold_silver_notes: Losses on metals cluster in regime changes and news weeks, which is precisely what an independent resample removes; expect real losing streaks on gold to be longer than the simulation shows. Resample results in R rather than money so the changing gold price and lot size do not distort the distribution. The long/short split is important on gold: a result carried entirely by longs during a rally is not evidence of an edge.

features.name: Demo acceptance harness: restart-survival test and demo-only build
features.description: A driver EA reads a phase file, attaches the EA under test through a generated .tpl with inputs, checks its persisted state, forces a lock (e.g. daily-loss), snapshots state and closes the terminal; after restart it verifies identical state and that the lock still blocks trading, then writes PASS/FAIL. A wrapper file defines DEMO_ONLY and includes the production source so test binaries refuse non-demo accounts.
features.rationale: Restart behaviour cannot be exercised in the Strategy Tester, and state loss or duplicate orders after a terminal restart are real account risks, so this is the right test before going live. It is heavy to build and maintain, though, and the in-tester state round trip covers most of the persistence logic for v1. The DEMO_ONLY wrapper is nearly free and worth adopting early, since it avoids forking the source for test builds.
features.gold_silver_notes: Not metal-specific, but worth running with both XAUUSD and XAGUSD instances attached so per-symbol state and locks are shown not to collide. Schedule one restart phase while the metals market is closed (daily break or weekend) and one while a position is open, since those are the situations a VPS reboot actually produces.

features.name: Count-based or drawdown-rescaled fitness formulas
features.description: Seen variants: wins/losses count ratio divided by (longest losing streak + 1), zeroed when TP < SL; and yearly return rescaled linearly to a fixed 5% maximum drawdown ('goodEnough'). Each collapses risk into one number through an untested assumption. If computed at all, write them as secondary report columns per parameter set; never use them as the optimisation target or for sizing.
features.rationale: Counting wins and losses ignores their size, so the formula rewards many small wins and hides the rare large loss; penalising streak length pushes the optimiser toward the same high-win-rate shapes. Rescaling return to a fixed drawdown assumes the historical maximum drawdown is the future bound and that return scales linearly with leverage; both are false, and the result is a leverage recommendation derived from the luckiest path. Both come from low-quality sources. The gated consistency criterion above does the job without these assumptions.
features.gold_silver_notes: These formulas favour exactly the profiles that are popular and fatal on gold: tight targets, wide or absent stops, grids and averaging, which show long winning runs until one news move or gap ends the account. Scaling a gold strategy up to a target drawdown implies leverage that a single gap through the stop can exceed several times over.

features.name: Composite 0-100 risk score as a control input
features.description: Weighted blend of 40% drawdown versus limit, 30% daily loss versus limit, 20% exposure versus caps and 10% spread versus maximum, renormalised over enabled components, proposed to scale lots or throttle entries. If shown at all, keep it a display-only column in the event log; enforce every limit separately as a hard gate.
features.rationale: A weighted average lets one breached limit be diluted by calm components: drawdown at 100% of its limit contributes only 40 points. The weights are arbitrary and become four more parameters to fit. Driving lot size from the score adds a feedback loop between risk state and sizing that is hard to reason about and hard to test. Independent hard limits, each with its own logged block reason, are simpler and safer.
features.gold_silver_notes: Spread carries only a tenth of the score, yet on metals a spread blowout at the daily break or on news is by itself sufficient reason not to trade. On gold and silver the spread check has to be a standalone gate, and so do drawdown and daily loss.

features.name: Staged optimisation switch (optimise sub-models one at a time)
features.description: A 'pass' input switches sub-models on one at a time (baseline, short model, long model, gate) so each stage is optimised with earlier parameters frozen instead of one large search. It shortens each run, but every stage is fitted to the same history and absorbs the noise the previous stage left behind; the combined set is never validated as a whole.
features.rationale: The mechanism exists to make a many-parameter, multi-model strategy optimisable, and needing it is itself the warning sign. Sequential fitting compounds selection bias while each individual run looks modest, so the total degrees of freedom are hidden from whoever reads the final report. A survival-first v1 should have few enough parameters to be searched and validated jointly. Low-quality single source.
features.gold_silver_notes: Separate long and short sub-models fitted on gold will encode the trend direction of the sample: the long model looks excellent across rally years and the gate stage then learns to switch the short model off. That is a description of the past, not a rule, and it fails when the regime turns. Silver's smaller trade count makes each stage even easier to fit to noise.

common_mistakes: Judging a trade from DEAL_PROFIT or a balance change alone, leaving out entry-deal commission, swap and partial closes, or treating a vanished ticket as proof of the outcome instead of rebuilding the position from its deals.
Measuring R against the trailed or final stop instead of the initial stop, which makes every breakeven-managed trade look risk-free.
Reporting results only in points or account money across years in which the gold price and lot sizes changed several-fold, instead of R or basis points.
Showing win rate without the breakeven win rate implied by the stop/target geometry and costs, so a near target passes for an edge.

Optimistic bar-replay assumptions: counting the target first when one bar contains both stop and target, ignoring costs or modelling them by shifting the entry, and trusting M1 bar spread that understates real reopen spread by roughly 3x.

Measuring execution quality only around the EA's own OrderSend call (GetTickCount, price sent versus price filled), which misses stop-loss and take-profit exits where slippage is worst, and logging slippage without a sign convention.
Sending push, email or web requests from OnTick or OnTradeTransaction, blocking the trade path and hitting notification rate limits during bursts.

Log spam from a condition that blocks trading on every tick, or the opposite fix of printing only every Nth message, which drops events arbitrarily; also decision logs that can be switched off entirely.
CSV logs that rewrite or duplicate the header on restart, are not flushed per row, cannot be read while open, or write duplicate rows after a restart; one file shared by several symbols or instances.

Silently replacing invalid inputs with defaults, or handling impossible parameter combinations by returning from OnTick so zero-trade passes stay in the optimiser results instead of rejecting them in OnInit.
Hard-coding the symbol name or pip value, so a broker suffix or a different contract/tick specification for gold or silver breaks sizing without any error.
Optimising on raw profit or an ad-hoc scalar (win/loss counts, streak penalties, return rescaled to a target drawdown) with no minimum trade count.
Treating an in-run in-sample/out-of-sample split as a true holdout even though the optimiser selects on the out-of-sample score too.
Deriving hour, weekday or session filters from bucket tables of the same backtest, often with a handful of trades per bucket, and mixing broker server time with UTC when tagging sessions.
Reading an independent-resample Monte Carlo drawdown as a worst case, and using backtest-derived Kelly fraction or similar statistics to set position size.
Folding independent risk limits into one weighted score so a breached limit is diluted by the others, then using the score to scale lots.
Splitting the strategy into sub-models and optimising them stage by stage on the same history, hiding the real number of fitted parameters.
Never comparing the strategy with a random-entry baseline using the same exits, so exit geometry and market drift are credited to the signal.
Not logging the inputs of the lot calculation or comparing planned risk with realised loss, so sizing errors and gap losses are only discovered from the equity curve.

Leaving restart and persistence behaviour untested because the Strategy Tester cannot exercise it, and letting tester-only code branches change trading behaviour rather than only UI, sleeps and notifications.
Storing per-trade diagnostics in the order comment, which brokers truncate or overwrite.
Drawing panels, objects and Comment output during optimisation, slowing every pass for no benefit.

features.name: Ownership by symbol + magic + position identifier
features.description: Every scan of positions, pendings and deals filters on symbol AND magic; once a position is known, track it by POSITION_IDENTIFIER/ticket, not by symbol. Never touch magic 0 (manual) or foreign magics. One explicit magic input per symbol/strategy instance (optionally base+offset per symbol), a separate magic for any secondary order class. Check ACCOUNT_MARGIN_MODE (netting vs hedging) at init.
features.rationale: Without strict ownership every other safeguard (recovery, flatten, stop repair) can act on trades it does not own. Cheap, deterministic and identical in tester and live. Keep the magic an explicit input: magics hashed from the symbol name (62248) can collide, and ones that encode the timeframe (7876) orphan positions when the chart timeframe changes. Comment matching (16136) is unreliable. Symbol-only tracking breaks on hedging accounts.
features.gold_silver_notes: Run XAUUSD and XAGUSD as separate instances with distinct magics so neither manages the other's trades. Filter on the chart's actual symbol name (brokers use suffixes or names such as GOLD), never a hard-coded string. Gold is the instrument people most often also trade by hand on the same account, so the 'never touch magic 0' rule matters in practice.

features.name: Stateless restart recovery from broker state
features.description: Treat the broker as the database. At init (after history sync) and cheaply each tick, re-derive state from positions, pending orders and HistorySelect filtered by symbol+magic: open position id, entry, pendings outstanding, last DEAL_ENTRY_IN time (already traded this session/day), last closed deal result, basket average. Allow an entry only when there is no own position, no own pending and no own entry deal since the signal/session start.
features.rationale: Most robust form of restart safety: no file or variable can go stale, it survives VPS migration, and the same code path runs in the tester and live, so it is honestly testable. Two limits to respect: history must be synced before it is trusted (see startup preflight), and some state is not derivable - 77639 restores initial risk from the current SL, which is wrong once the stop has been moved; that part needs the durable store.
features.gold_silver_notes: Session-breakout gold logic (London/NY open) places a bracket once per day; a VPS or terminal restart inside the window must not place a second one. Metals have a daily break and a weekend gap where terminals restart or reconnect, so recovery runs often. Make the history lookback cover the longest holding/session window (77060 uses 7 days).

features.name: Persisted once-per-signal entry lock (GlobalVariable)
features.description: After a filled entry (or just before sending), write a 'no new entry before <end of signal bar>' timestamp to a terminal GlobalVariable keyed by login+symbol+timeframe+magic+direction, then GlobalVariablesFlush. Refuse entries while TimeCurrent() is below it. Give tester keys a suffix and delete them on deinit. Use it as a second line behind the deal-history check, never as the only duplicate guard.
features.rationale: Seen in 7 EAs and cheap, but it duplicates what deal history states authoritatively. GlobalVariables are terminal-local (lost on VPS migration or reinstall), are purged after about four weeks without access and can be deleted by hand. Worth having as a write-ahead marker for the short window before history is synced and to block same-bar re-entry after a stop-out; not a v1 requirement if the history-derived guard exists.
features.gold_silver_notes: Gold frequently stops a trade out inside the same signal bar on a spike; the lock stops an immediate re-entry on that same signal. Include the symbol in the key so gold and silver locks are independent. Prefer bar-end time over a fixed cooldown in seconds (7694 uses 15 s, which is meaningless on H1 gold).

features.name: Minimal durable store for non-derivable state
features.description: Persist only what the broker cannot tell you: per-ticket initial volume, initial risk, last executed partial-TP/breakeven stage, day baseline, flatten latch. Use GlobalVariables keyed by login+symbol+magic+ticket, written on change (or when dirty, at most every 30 s), followed by GlobalVariablesFlush outside the tester, deleted when the position closes; files via temp-file-then-FileMove. On load, drop keys without a live position. OnDeinit saves state for every REASON_* and never flattens.
features.rationale: Without it a restart re-fires a partial-TP level, recomputes percentages from the reduced volume, loses the R basis for management, or forgets that a flatten was in progress. Keep the surface minimal so there is little to corrupt, and save nothing before the account is ready. 13942 flattens on chart/parameter change; persist instead. Tester keys must be isolated so backtests do not read live state.
features.gold_silver_notes: Partial-TP ladders and breakeven stages are the usual management style on gold. With a 0.01 minimum lot and coarse volume steps on metals, a level re-fired on the already reduced volume either fails the volume check or closes more than intended. Store initial risk at entry because the current SL no longer shows it once the stop has been trailed.

features.name: Transaction-confirmed order state machine (in-flight guard + deferred deal queue)
features.description: After a send returning DONE/PLACED, store the order ticket and block new entry logic until OnTradeTransaction delivers a DEAL_ADD with matching order, symbol and magic; on timeout, poll positions/history instead of waiting forever. Queue DEAL_ADD events until the deal and its order are selectable in history, then update realised P/L, loss streak, cooldown and delete sibling OCO pendings. Open a reversal only after the closing deal is confirmed.
features.rationale: Directly prevents duplicate entries on asynchronous fills, the most common live-only bug in these EAs. Events are a hint, not the source of truth: they are missed while disconnected, and a waiting flag without a timeout can block the bot indefinitely (63916 bounds the wait at 3x1000 ms, 79437 falls back after 10 s). 79437's deferred queue fixes the race where the deal is not yet selectable. Always pair with a startup resync (48222 lacks it).
features.gold_silver_notes: During gold news spikes fills arrive late or partially, which is when a second send slips through. A two-sided breakout bracket must lose its opposite pending as soon as one side fills, or a whipsaw fills both. Use loss-streak counters only for cooldown or risk reduction, never to scale lots up (21511 and 63569 feed martingale sizing).

features.name: Closed-bar gate that re-arms on data failure
features.description: Detect a new bar on the signal timeframe (SeriesInfoInteger SERIES_LASTBAR_DATE, iTime or CopyTime), not the chart timeframe, and read every feature from shift 1 only. Advance the processed-bar latch only after all CopyBuffer/CopyRates/tick refreshes and the trade-permission check succeed; otherwise set a recount flag so the same closed bar is re-evaluated on the next tick while it is still the last closed bar.
features.rationale: Closed-bar evaluation removes intra-bar look-ahead and repainting, so 'open prices' or 1-minute-OHLC tests match live behaviour - the basis of honest testing. Committing the latch only after valid data avoids the silent 'signal skipped on cold start' bug that 14 EAs work around. The re-arm must cover data and permission failures only, not order failures (see bounded delivery).
features.gold_silver_notes: After the metals daily break and the Monday open, the first tick often arrives before higher-timeframe buffers are recalculated; on a fresh VPS, H1/H4 history for XAGUSD may not be loaded at all. Closed-bar-only logic also makes gold results much less sensitive to tick-data quality and spread modelling in the tester.

features.name: Decide once, deliver with a bounded retry window and failure circuit breaker
features.description: Evaluate the signal once at bar close and store it as a pending intent (bar time, direction). Retry delivery only while that bar is still the last closed bar; stop on DONE/DONE_PARTIAL/PLACED. Retry only transient retcodes (requote, price changed, busy), never invalid stops, no money or market closed. Cap attempts, enforce a minimum interval between sends, and pause entries after N consecutive failures. One-shot actions like breakeven are attempted once.
features.rationale: 78343 is the best version. The naive form in six sources (10281, 8595, 8499, 11102, 17137 rewind the bar stamp on any OrderSend/OrderModify failure; 1397 commits only on success) retries every tick with no cap and no error classification and re-runs steps that already succeeded - popular but harmful: request floods on permanent errors and late fills from a stale signal. 78715's mark-before-act is the safe at-most-once extreme. Bounded delivery plus the in-flight guard gives retries without duplicates.
features.gold_silver_notes: On gold, requotes, off-quotes and rejected stops cluster around news and the daily rollover, exactly when a per-tick retry does the most damage and a late fill is furthest from the decision price. On H1 and above, add a time limit inside the bar: a retry 40 minutes after the signal is a different trade.

features.name: Market/indicator data sanity and history-readiness guards
features.description: Before any decision require: BarsCalculated(handle) at least the indicator period, Copy* returned exactly the requested count, values finite and above zero, signal-timeframe history loaded and Bars above a minimum. Add plausibility bounds as fractions of price: ATR below about 10%, stop distance below about 2% before lot sizing. Any failure aborts the tick with a logged reason; a getter returns 0 and the caller refuses to trade.
features.rationale: Garbage indicator values on a cold start or after a history gap are a direct path to absurd lot sizes or false signals. The bounds are sanity limits, not tuning knobs: keep them wide, fixed and out of the optimiser. Every failure must be logged so a 'no trades' backtest can be explained rather than hidden.
features.gold_silver_notes: Risk-based sizing divides by the stop distance: a zero or tiny ATR on gold becomes an oversized lot on an instrument with a large tick value. Express bounds as a fraction of price, not points, because brokers quote gold with 2 or 3 digits and silver with 3 or more. Silver's ATR relative to price is larger than gold's, so do not reuse gold's bounds unchecked.

features.name: Input validation and fail-fast init with a hard risk cap
features.description: OnInit returns INIT_PARAMETERS_INCORRECT for out-of-range or inconsistent inputs: risk per trade above a compiled-in ceiling (e.g. 2%), non-positive RR or periods, fast >= slow, session hours not strictly ordered, trailing step above trailing start. It returns INIT_FAILED when an indicator handle, required file or the symbol's filling mode cannot be set. In the tester the same check ends the pass so the optimiser skips nonsensical combinations.
features.rationale: Costs almost nothing and prevents the two worst operator errors: oversized risk and inverted or overlapping session settings. Ending invalid passes early also keeps the optimiser from wasting passes on, and occasionally 'finding', nonsensical combinations. Per-side open/close enable switches (15228) belong here as plain inputs and give an exit-only mode for winding the bot down.
features.gold_silver_notes: Compile the risk ceiling in rather than exposing it; gold's volatility makes a mistyped risk input (10 instead of 1.0) account-ending. Session hours are in broker server time, which differs between brokers, so validate ordering and log the interpreted window. Filling mode (FOK/IOC) for metals differs by broker; set it from the symbol at init.

features.name: Startup preflight: connection, permissions and account identity
features.description: Do not load state, save state or trade until the terminal is connected, ACCOUNT_LOGIN is valid, balance and equity are positive, server time is sane (after a fixed date) and a few seconds have passed for history sync. Gate every send on TERMINAL_TRADE_ALLOWED, MQL_TRADE_ALLOWED and ACCOUNT_TRADE_EXPERT, alerting once when one turns off. If the login differs from the stored one, reinitialise state. Retry readiness from the timer.
features.rationale: State loaded or a baseline captured while disconnected is silently wrong and then persisted - 78680 and 73870 exist to stop exactly that. Checking permissions only in OnInit (12641, 14773) is not enough: AutoTrading can be switched off later, so gate each send and alert once. An account switch on the same terminal must not inherit the previous account's day lock or ticket state.
features.gold_silver_notes: Metals close for a daily break and the weekend, and terminals are often restarted then, starting disconnected with zero balance or an unset server time. A baseline or lock captured in that state gives a wrong daily-loss limit for the whole next gold session.

features.name: Single-instance lock with heartbeat
features.description: Claim an owner GlobalVariable per login+symbol+magic atomically with GlobalVariableSetOnCondition, store the chart ID and refresh a heartbeat every second from the timer. A second copy refuses to start unless the heartbeat is older than about 10 s; a copy that loses ownership stops trading and removes itself; the owner releases the lock on deinit. Skip the lock in the tester.
features.rationale: Protects against the operator error of attaching the bot twice to the same symbol and magic, which can double entries in the same tick before either instance sees the other's position. Only 2 EAs (both good quality) and it adds its own failure mode (stale lock, clock source), so keep it behind a flag; ownership filtering plus the in-flight guard already limit the damage. Not meaningful in the tester.
features.gold_silver_notes: Key the lock per symbol+magic so the XAUUSD and XAGUSD instances coexist. Drive the heartbeat from local time on a timer: server time and ticks stop during the metals daily break, and a tick-driven heartbeat would look dead.

features.name: Trading-day rollover: baseline rebuild and daily state reset
features.description: Trading-day index = (server time − resetHour*3600)/86400. On rollover reset daily flags and the phase machine (range locked, orders placed once, managed, expired), delete leftover pendings and capture the day-start balance. If no saved baseline exists (mid-day start, state loss), rebuild it as current balance minus today's buy/sell deal profit+swap+commission+fee, excluding balance operations, and flag it as estimated. Capture only when time and balance are valid.
features.rationale: A daily loss limit is only as good as its baseline: using the current balance at a mid-day restart silently resets the limit after losses (the survival failure 78680 and 79035 fix). The estimate from history must be flagged because floating P/L at day start cannot be fully reconstructed. The phase machine with 'orders placed once' keeps a session strategy from re-arming. 64444's refresh-after-N-bars adds a tunable parameter; prefer a fixed expiry tied to the session.
features.gold_silver_notes: Gold's liquid day starts after the roughly one-hour rollover break; broker server midnight and a prop firm's reset time often differ, so the reset hour must be an operator setting taken from the rule set, not an optimised parameter. Swap is part of the deal sum and must be included. Leftover breakout pendings from yesterday's range must not survive into today's session.

features.name: Idempotent SL/TP reconciliation and missing-stop repair
features.description: Each cycle, for every owned position compute the intended SL/TP from the open price and stored initial risk, and send a modify only when it differs from the current value by more than a tolerance (tolerant double compare, normalised to tick size). A position found with SL equal to zero is repaired at once. One-shot moves such as breakeven are attempted once per stage to avoid retry storms.
features.rationale: A position without a stop is unbounded risk; a convergence loop (desired vs actual) repairs it after restarts, failed first modifies and stop-less opens without having to track what failed. The tolerance compare (12220) avoids 'no changes' rejections and per-tick modify spam; 77639's attempt-once rule for breakeven avoids retry storms. Deterministic and identical in the tester.
features.gold_silver_notes: On market-execution accounts metals orders can be rejected or opened without SL/TP in the opening request, so stops are attached after the fill; a gold position without a stop through a news release is the largest single tail risk. Compare using SYMBOL_TRADE_TICK_SIZE (gold and silver differ) and respect stops/freeze levels, which widen around news.

features.name: Latched flatten: close-all retried until flat
features.description: When a close-all condition fires (daily loss limit, session end, profit/loss flush), set a 'flattening' latch and persist it. While set, each tick/timer cycle first deletes owned pendings and closes owned positions, evaluates nothing else and blocks new entries. The latch clears only when owned position and pending counts are both zero; then state is reset and the realised result is logged.
features.rationale: Close-all loops partially fail in practice (requote, busy, market closed). Without a latch the trigger condition can disappear after the first partial close (profit falls back below target, equity recovers) and the rest is left open - a hidden-risk state. Three EAs use the same simple latch. Persist it so a restart continues flattening, and delete pendings so they cannot fill mid-flatten.
features.gold_silver_notes: Closes fail when the metals market is in its daily break or liquidity vanishes at news; a one-shot close-all then leaves a partial gold book. The latch keeps trying at reopen. Trigger time-based flattening (Friday, pre-break) with enough margin that retries can still succeed before the market closes.

features.name: Timer plus tick processing with throttle
features.description: Run risk guards, in-flight timeouts, stop reconciliation, state saves and heartbeat from both OnTick and a 1-second OnTimer through one shared function; throttle heavy management to once every few seconds. Keep signal evaluation on the closed-bar gate only, so timer cadence never changes trading decisions and tester results do not depend on timer granularity.
features.rationale: Guards that live only in OnTick stop when the chart symbol is quiet; a 1-second timer costs nothing. The discipline is to keep decisions off the timer: 244 runs all logic from the timer with a price-change gate, which makes results depend on timer granularity and tick modelling. Throttling (18709) reduces modify and request spam.
features.gold_silver_notes: A single instance managing both metals only gets OnTick for the chart symbol; silver can move while the gold chart is momentarily quiet. During the daily break no ticks arrive at all, yet timeouts, heartbeats and the day rollover still need to run.

features.name: Edge-triggered health monitoring, heartbeat and self-audit
features.description: Compute boolean health states (connected, algo trading allowed, expected login, owned position without SL, day-loss lock, margin) and notify only when a state changes, including recovery. Key each issue: alert once, forget when it clears, persist keys across restarts. Add a daily status heartbeat, an OnDeinit 'stopped' message, a per symbol|magic|direction duplicate-position count, and a startup scan of deals since a stored last-seen time.
features.rationale: Does not change trading decisions, so it can follow v1, but the edge-triggered pattern is the right way to log state changes from day one (alert once, report recovery). The self-audit checks are independent verification that the dedup and ownership logic actually worked. Push notifications cannot be validated in the tester; test them on demo.
features.gold_silver_notes: A stop-out or an unexpected open while the terminal was offline through a gold news spike is what the offline-gap scan reveals. Duplicate positions matter more on gold because margin and loss per lot are large. A 'position without SL' health state should be the highest-priority alert for metals.

features.name: External data (news calendar) fetch robustness
features.description: Fetch calendar/news data from a timer, never per tick. Cache it in a date-stamped local file and reuse the file on restart; refresh on a fixed interval after success and retry sooner after failure. Distinguish 'URL not whitelisted' (error 4060), transport errors and non-200 HTTP codes with actionable messages. Show the last-success timestamp and state explicitly what the bot does when the data is stale.
features.rationale: Only needed if a news filter is added. The honest-testing problem is the main reason to defer it: WebRequest and the built-in calendar do not work in the Strategy Tester, so the filter's effect cannot be verified by backtest unless historical events are replayed from a file. If added, failures must be loud. The raw idea is MQL4 (error 4060); in MQL5 a non-whitelisted URL returns error 4014.
features.gold_silver_notes: Gold and silver react most to US CPI, NFP and FOMC; if the calendar fetch fails silently, the one filter meant to cover those events is off without anyone knowing. Because the filter cannot run in the Strategy Tester, report backtests with it disabled as the honest baseline.

features.name: Fragile state carriers and hidden persisted settings/learned state
features.description: Keeping bot state or ownership in order comments, chart-object properties, 'position already has an SL' heuristics or balance snapshots, and persisting settings or learned tables that silently override the inputs. Comments get truncated or rewritten, chart objects vanish with the chart, balance moves with deposits and other EAs, and hidden persisted parameters make live behaviour differ from what was tested. Use magic+ticket-keyed state and deal history instead.
features.rationale: Each of these looked convenient in its source EA and each hides risk. Comment tags (71583, 16136) and SL-presence (51095) misidentify what the bot owns; chart objects (12598) disappear with a template change; balance snapshots (7891) confuse deposits, swaps and other EAs' trades with the bot's own result and were used for lot escalation. Persisted settings (75690, 19752) and learned tables (1108) make live behaviour irreproducible from the inputs and let tester pre-training leak into live.
features.gold_silver_notes: Partial closes, routine in gold ladders, are where many brokers rewrite the comment (the reader of 71583 notes its comment-tag design would not work as written). A balance snapshot misreads swap charges and deposits as losses. Learned tables pre-trained in the tester on gold's trending years are curve fitting carried into live.

common_mistakes: Keeping trade state only in memory (static/global variables): a restart re-enters on the same bar or session, re-fires a partial-TP level, or orphans open positions.
Consuming the new-bar latch before indicator data and quotes are validated, so the bar's signal is silently skipped on a cold start or failed CopyBuffer.
The opposite error: rewinding the bar stamp on any OrderSend/OrderModify failure, which retries every tick with no attempt cap and no error classification and re-runs steps that already succeeded.

Sending a new order before the previous one is confirmed (treating the OrderSend return as proof a position exists), giving duplicate entries on asynchronous fills; or using a waiting flag with no timeout, which can block the bot forever.
Reading a deal inside OnTradeTransaction before it and its order are selectable in history, and relying on events alone with no polling reconciliation or startup resync.
Scanning by symbol only, or by comment or 'has an SL', and so managing manual trades or another EA's trades; counting open positions but forgetting pending orders when enforcing one-trade-at-a-time.
Auto-deriving the magic number from symbol characters or timeframe: collisions between symbols, and orphaned positions when the chart timeframe changes.

Capturing the day-start baseline while disconnected (zero balance, unset server time) or taking the current balance as baseline on a mid-day restart, which silently resets the daily loss limit; counting deposits/withdrawals as trading P/L.

Writing GlobalVariables without GlobalVariablesFlush (lost on a crash), never deleting per-ticket keys, sharing keys between tester and live, and saving state before the account is ready so good state is overwritten with garbage.
Using a GlobalVariable or a fixed seconds cooldown as the only duplicate-entry guard; it is lost on VPS migration and a 15-second cooldown confirms nothing.
Recomputing partial-close percentages from the already reduced volume after a restart, and restoring 'initial risk' from the current SL after it has been trailed or moved to breakeven.
One-shot close-all that is not retried: a partial failure leaves a half-flattened book, and entry logic keeps running while the flatten is incomplete.
Flattening positions in OnDeinit on chart, timeframe or parameter change instead of persisting state and resuming.
Trading on unvalidated indicator values (zero ATR, EMPTY_VALUE, too few bars, unsynchronised higher timeframe), which turns risk-based sizing into absurd lots.
No input validation and no hard risk ceiling: the optimiser explores nonsensical combinations and an operator typo becomes oversized risk.

Running all guards only in OnTick, so loss limits, timeouts and stop repair freeze when the chart symbol is quiet or the market is in its break; or the reverse, putting trading decisions on the timer so results depend on timer granularity.
Re-sending SL/TP modifies every tick with exact double comparison, or retrying a rejected breakeven indefinitely, producing 'no changes' errors and request storms.
Using new-bar detection on the chart timeframe when the signal timeframe is different.
Using loss detection or streak state to escalate lot size (martingale) rather than to cool down or reduce risk.
Level-triggered alerts on every tick instead of edge-triggered alerts with recovery messages, so real failures drown in spam; no signal when the bot itself stops.
External news data fetched per tick or per restart with no cache, WebRequest whitelist errors not distinguished from transport errors, and stale data not visible - the filter silently stops working.
Checking trade permissions only in OnInit and never again, and allowing a second instance on the same symbol and magic with no instance lock.

features.name: Operating-mode switch (Normal / Monitor-only / Exit-only / Flatten-and-idle)
features.description: One enum run mode read by every entry and management path: NORMAL, MONITOR (compute and log signals, send nothing), EXIT_ONLY (no new entries, keep managing stops and exits), FLATTEN (close own-magic positions, delete own pendings, then idle). Gate entries in a single CanOpen() function. Expose it as an input and a chart button, log every change, and show the mode on the dashboard.
features.rationale: A single gate is the simplest reliable manual kill-switch and gives a safe wind-down without detaching the EA, which would abandon open-trade management. MONITOR mode also allows a live dry run that can be compared with the tester. It does not touch strategy logic, so it adds no curve-fitting surface.
features.gold_silver_notes: Use EXIT_ONLY ahead of scheduled US data (NFP, CPI, FOMC) and into the Friday close, since metals gap over weekends. XAUUSD and XAGUSD normally run as separate instances but are strongly correlated; an operator standing down usually wants both, so consider one shared mode key for the pair.

features.name: Independent long/short enable switches
features.description: Two bool inputs, AllowLong and AllowShort, checked in the same entry gate as the run mode. They block new entries on one side only; open positions on a disabled side stay managed to their stops and exits. Keep per-direction position counters so each side's limits work alone. Test and report both sides separately as well as together.
features.rationale: Cheap operational control and a diagnostic that shows whether the edge exists on both sides. The risk is using it as an optimised parameter, so it must be fixed before testing and never tuned to the sample.
features.gold_silver_notes: Gold's long upward drift in recent years makes long-only look excellent in backtests; switching shorts off on that basis is curve fitting to one regime. Use the switches for diagnostics and operations, and report each side separately for both XAU and XAG.

features.name: Panic flatten button with retry-until-flat and result report
features.description: OBJ_BUTTON handled in OnChartEvent (CHARTEVENT_OBJECT_CLICK, matched by object name) so it works without ticks. Pressing sets a FLATTEN latch; OnTimer and OnTick loop PositionsTotal() and OrdersTotal() backwards, filtering by magic and symbol, closing with CTrade and deleting pendings, until none remain. Check every retcode, cap retries per second, report closed versus failed counts, then release the latch and stay idle.
features.rationale: The one manual control that directly limits loss. Most source versions fire once and never verify the result; the latched retry (48267) and the closed/failed report (62811, 67011) are what make it trustworthy. Popular (7 EAs) and in this case also worth having, provided it is scoped to the bot's own magic.
features.gold_silver_notes: Metals have a daily trading break (typically about an hour around 17:00 New York) and a weekend closure: the click is received but close requests are rejected, so the latch must persist and retry at reopen and the panel must say the close is pending. Expect slippage on XAU around news and on thinner XAG. Filter by _Symbol, because broker names vary (XAUUSD, GOLD, suffixes).

features.name: Two-step confirmation for destructive buttons
features.description: First click arms the action: button text changes to CONFIRM, a timestamp is stored, and the arm expires after about 5 seconds via OnTimer. Second click inside the window executes. Show how many positions and pendings will be affected in the button or status label. Prefer this over MessageBox, which is modal and stalls the EA while it waits for an answer.
features.rationale: A flatten button with no guard will eventually be mis-clicked; a guard that blocks the EA thread is worse because stops and trailing stop being serviced. The two-click arm from 73870 costs a few lines and has neither problem.
features.gold_silver_notes: Gold can move several dollars in the seconds around a release. Keep the arm window short and the confirmation non-blocking so position management keeps running while the operator decides.

features.name: Selective bulk close with scope selector
features.description: One close routine taking a filter: side (buys or sells), pendings only, this symbol or all symbols of this magic. Reuse the panic-flatten loop and its closed/failed report, and put the buttons behind the same confirmation step. Leave out the profit-only and loss-only filters seen in the sources: closing winners while keeping losers is a discretionary habit that worsens the loss distribution.
features.rationale: Side and pendings-only scopes are legitimate operator tools, but the full flatten already covers the emergency case, so this is not needed in v1. The profit-sign filters are common in close-all utilities and should not be carried over.
features.gold_silver_notes: With XAU and XAG both running, the useful scopes are 'this symbol' and 'both metals for this bot'. Per-side closing only matters on hedging accounts; a netting account holds one net position per symbol.

features.name: Self-removal hard stop via ExpertRemove()
features.description: After a hard stop (for example a max-drawdown breach) and only once position and pending counts for the magic are confirmed zero, log the reason, send a notification and call ExpertRemove() so the bot cannot re-enter until a human re-attaches it. Pair it with a persisted halt flag, otherwise re-attaching or a terminal restart silently resumes trading.
features.rationale: The firmest stop available, because no bot code runs afterwards, but it also removes the dashboard and any remaining management and is undone by a simple re-attach. A persisted halt latch gives the same protection with fewer side effects, so keep this as an optional final step. In the Strategy Tester it ends the pass, which makes a breach visible instead of averaged away. Only one low-quality source.
features.gold_silver_notes: Suited to a drawdown breach caused by a gold gap or spike, where automatic re-entry into the same conditions is the main danger. Confirm flat first: during the metals daily break the close may still be pending.

features.name: Status dashboard with block reason and limit usage
features.description: Small OBJ_LABEL panel refreshed on a 1-second timer, not every tick: run mode and the current no-trade reason, own-magic position count and floating P/L, equity and drawdown percent, used versus limit for each risk rule with time to daily reset, live spread, time to bar close, last event. Read-only. Skip drawing when MQL_OPTIMIZATION is set or in non-visual tests.
features.rationale: An operator who cannot see why the bot is idle will override or restart it. Showing the block reason and how much of each limit is used is the minimum for supervised live running. Being read-only, it cannot make live behaviour differ from the test; it must cost nothing during optimisation.
features.gold_silver_notes: Show spread in points and in money per lot: XAU spread widens sharply at rollover and around US data, and XAG is wider relative to price. Avoid the word 'pips', since digits for XAUUSD and XAGUSD differ by broker. Name the block reason (spread, news, session break, daily limit).

features.name: Once-per-event alerts and push notifications
features.description: On state transitions only (limit hit, halt, flatten result, blackout entered, order failure) write a log line, raise Alert and, if enabled, SendNotification. Remember the last event id or state so each event fires once, not every tick. Respect SendNotification's rate limits (about 2 per second, 10 per minute) by dropping repeats. Disable in the tester.
features.rationale: Risk-limit and halt events need a human quickly, and a once-per-transition alert is cheap. The sources that work remember the event index (16308) or emit from one Event() function (79372); alerting without that memory spams every tick.
features.gold_silver_notes: Limit hits and failed closes on metals cluster around US releases and rollover. One message per event matters here: a gold spike can otherwise produce a burst that exhausts the push rate limit just when the message is needed.

features.name: News event lines and blackout label on chart
features.description: For each event the news filter already uses, draw an OBJ_VLINE at the event time, coloured by impact and named with currency, importance and title, plus a label stating which event is pausing trading and until when. Draw from the same event list the filter uses, never a second source, and delete lines after the event passes. Display only; it changes no decision.
features.rationale: Explains a pause at a glance, but only has value once a news filter exists and its data can be trusted; the lines themselves change nothing. All three sources are quality-2 templates, so take the idea and not the code.
features.gold_silver_notes: Both metals react mainly to USD events (NFP, CPI, FOMC), so show the USD high-impact events the filter actually uses. Check event times against broker server time; a wrong offset misleads the operator about when the blackout applies.

features.name: Runtime strategy overrides, per-ticket toggles and manual trade buttons
features.description: Chart buttons that change lot, SL or TP, switch trailing, breakeven or partial close on and off, toggle them per ticket, or fire manual buy and sell while the bot runs. If any manual action is kept, restrict it to risk-reducing ones (move stop to breakeven, close), route it through the same guarded execution function as automated orders, and log it.
features.rationale: Every runtime override makes the live system different from the one that was tested, and the change is rarely logged, so results can no longer be attributed to the strategy. Manual entries under the bot's magic contaminate its statistics, and per-ticket toggles multiply the states to reason about. Seen in three EAs of quality 2-3; popularity here reflects manual-trader convenience, not robustness. The one good point (79285) is the shared guarded execution path.
features.gold_silver_notes: Gold's fast moves tempt operators to widen a stop or switch off trailing mid-trade, which is how a tested risk profile is lost. A manual lot bump on XAG is especially costly because the contract is typically 5000 oz.

features.name: Remote command queue with acknowledgement
features.description: OnTimer polls an endpoint with WebRequest every N seconds for a command row (account, symbol or ALL, action, value), executes it once, then posts SUCCESS or FAILED with details. Accept only risk-reducing actions (halt, flatten, breakeven), verify the account number and a shared secret, ignore stale or repeated command ids, and keep trading safely when the endpoint is unreachable.
features.rationale: The pattern is sound (execute once, acknowledge with the outcome), but it adds a network dependency, a blocking WebRequest, URL whitelisting and an attack surface on a live account. Worth adding later, limited to risk-reducing commands and off by default. Only one source.
features.gold_silver_notes: Useful for standing down before a scheduled release when away from the terminal. A polling delay of N seconds is far too slow to react to a gold spike, so it never replaces stops held at the broker.

features.name: User-drawn chart objects as trigger levels and direction switches
features.description: OnChartEvent tracks creation, deletion and dragging of trendlines or level lines, keeps a registry with armed and fired state, reads the line price at the current bar (ObjectGetValueByTime in MQL5) and fires once on a cross; arrows or line width encode direction and armed state. Acceptable only as alert-only tooling outside the automated bot.
features.rationale: It makes the bot discretionary and unreproducible: hand-drawn levels cannot be backtested, state lives in fragile object properties (line width, deleted arrows), and a template change or accidental drag alters trading behaviour. Fine for a manual trader, wrong for a bot that must be honestly testable.
features.gold_silver_notes: Hand-drawn gold levels (round numbers, prior highs) are popular, but a line-cross trigger during a spike fills well away from the line, and none of it shows up in a backtest.

features.name: Manual pre-trade risk calculator (linked lines, fields and R:R)
features.description: Draggable entry, SL and TP lines linked both ways to edit fields: dragging (CHARTEVENT_OBJECT_DRAG) recomputes lot, money at risk and reward; editing money or points moves the lines; TP can follow SL by a reward-to-risk ratio. Compute money with OrderCalcProfit or tick value and tick size, and round lots to the volume step. Build it as a separate tool, not inside the EA.
features.rationale: A sound manual-trading aid, and its sizing arithmetic is the same the bot needs, but an automated bot sizes from its own stop distance. Keeping the panel separate keeps UI code out of the trading path. Best reference is 1637 (quality 4).
features.gold_silver_notes: Must use the symbol's own tick value, tick size and contract size: XAUUSD is typically 100 oz and XAGUSD 5000 oz per lot, so the same point distance means very different money. Check volume step and stops level per broker.

features.name: Chart markers for next trailing-stop level and broker minimum stop distance
features.description: Draw one marker at the level the trailing logic would move the stop to next, and one at the nearest stop the broker accepts (price minus or plus SYMBOL_TRADE_STOPS_LEVEL, also respecting SYMBOL_TRADE_FREEZE_LEVEL). Update on new bar or timer. Lets the operator see why a stop modification was skipped. Live and visual-mode only.
features.rationale: Cheap diagnostic that explains skipped or rejected stop modifications. Not needed for correctness, because the stop-level check itself belongs in the execution code. One quality-2 source.
features.gold_silver_notes: Stops and freeze levels on metals vary by broker, and some report 0 while still rejecting stops that sit too close. The marker makes a refused stop move on XAU visible instead of silent.

features.name: Chart hygiene: instance-scoped object names, prefix-only cleanup, restore chart
features.description: Name every object with a fixed tag plus ChartID() and magic so several instances never collide. In OnDeinit delete with ObjectsDeleteAll(0, prefix) only, never all objects. Preferably change no chart properties; if any are changed in OnInit, save them first and restore them in OnDeinit. Keep the UI in one module that a single input can switch off.
features.rationale: Basic good behaviour that prevents cross-instance bugs and stops the EA deleting the user's own drawings. It costs almost nothing if done from the first line and is painful to retrofit.
features.gold_silver_notes: A metals bot usually runs one instance on XAUUSD and one on XAGUSD in the same terminal; scoped names stop one instance deleting or overwriting the other's panel.

features.name: Persist operator control state across restarts
features.description: Save run mode, halt and flatten latches and any operator toggles to terminal GlobalVariables whenever they change, followed by GlobalVariablesFlush, and restore them in OnInit. Scope keys by account login, symbol and magic. GlobalVariables hold doubles only and expire after four weeks without access, so re-write them periodically. Persist control state only; strategy parameters stay in inputs.
features.rationale: A kill-switch that forgets it was pressed after a restart, timeframe change or VPS reboot is not a kill-switch. The sources persist panel convenience settings; the valuable use is the halt state. Restricting persistence to control state leaves the tested parameters untouched.
features.gold_silver_notes: Terminals get restarted at VPS reboots and over the weekend. A halt set on Friday after a loss limit must still be in force at the weekly reopen, when metals gaps are most likely.

features.name: Optimisation-run dashboard widgets
features.description: Chart widgets (multi-series plot, table, progress bar) updated as optimisation passes arrive, showing the share of profitable versus losing passes. The useful idea is judging the whole distribution of passes instead of the best one. Keep it as a separate analysis tool or read the optimiser's exported results; do not put it in the trading EA.
features.rationale: Looking at the distribution of passes is healthy, but live widgets add code with no trading value, and the tester's own results table and export already hold the data. Out of scope for v1; one source.
features.gold_silver_notes: An optimisation over a single trending gold period shows many profitable passes for reasons unrelated to the strategy, so a pass-ratio display flatters the system. Check silver and out-of-sample periods separately.

common_mistakes: Close-all that fires once and never checks the result: no retcode handling, no retry, no closed-versus-failed report, so the operator believes the account is flat when it is not.
Close-all utilities that close everything on the account instead of filtering by magic and symbol, killing manual trades and other EAs' positions.
Kill actions driven from OnTick, so nothing happens when no ticks arrive; conversely, assuming a button that works without ticks can also close positions while the market is shut.
Destructive buttons with no confirmation, or a MessageBox confirmation that blocks the EA while positions are open.
Kill-switch implemented only as an input flag (e.g. ShutDown.NOW): it needs the properties dialog, re-runs OnInit, and if left on it keeps closing every new trade.
Control state held only in chart objects (button state, line width, deleted arrows) and lost on timeframe change, template load or restart; no persistence of a halt.
Object names without an instance prefix and cleanup that deletes all chart objects, including the user's drawings; chart properties changed and not restored.
Manual buttons and runtime toggles that bypass the bot's risk checks or are not logged, so the live system is no longer the one that was tested.
Offering 'close profitable only' as a bulk action, which institutionalises cutting winners and holding losers.
Dashboards redrawn on every tick and left running in optimisation, slowing tests; panels that show P/L but not why trading is blocked, or show account-wide figures instead of the bot's own magic.
Alerts and push notifications raised on every tick instead of once per event, running into SendNotification rate limits.
Calling ExpertRemove() before confirming the account is flat, leaving positions with no management.
Remote control without authentication or idempotency, able to open trades, and polled in a way that blocks the trading thread.
Letting hand-drawn lines or arrows drive entries: untestable in the Strategy Tester and changed by an accidental drag.
GlobalVariable keys not scoped by account, symbol and magic, so instances overwrite each other's saved state; forgetting the four-week expiry.
Displaying 'pips' and money values with hard-coded point assumptions, which are wrong on metals where digits and contract size differ by broker and between gold and silver.
